+from source_utils import (
+    ROOT,
+    load_members_and_folds,
+    require_physical_scratch,
+    sha256_file,
+    verify_recipe_sources,
+    verify_train_footer,
+    write_json,
+)
+
+from wnn.data import SEQUENCE_LENGTH, WARMUP, SequenceFile
+
+ARMS = ("raw", "raw_plus_clock", "raw_plus_group_states")
+
+
+def _sha256_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
+    """Hash in-memory serialized configuration bytes."""
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _feature_arms(sequence: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
+    """Prepare three matched representations for rows at and after warmup."""
+    raw, clock, group_states = extract_online_features(sequence)
+    return {
+        "raw": raw,
+        "raw_plus_clock": np.concatenate((raw, clock), axis=1),
+        "raw_plus_group_states": np.concatenate((raw, group_states), axis=1),
+    }
+
+
+def _verify_prefix_invariants(sequence: np.ndarray, first_outputs: dict[str, np.ndarray]) -> None:
+    """Check prefix causality against truncation and future perturbation."""
+    prefix_length = 2_000
+    prefix_outputs = _feature_arms(sequence[:prefix_length])
+    future_perturbed = sequence.copy()
+    future_perturbed[prefix_length:] += 17.0
+    perturbed_outputs = _feature_arms(future_perturbed)
+    prefix_rows = prefix_length - WARMUP
+    for arm in ARMS:
+        if not (
+            np.array_equal(first_outputs[arm][:prefix_rows], prefix_outputs[arm])
+            and np.array_equal(
+                first_outputs[arm][:prefix_rows], perturbed_outputs[arm][:prefix_rows]
+            )
+        ):
+            raise AssertionError(f"prefix/future-perturbation invariance failed for {arm}")
+
+
+def _fit_all_folds(
+    source: SequenceFile,
+    members: list[dict[str, int]],
+    fold_by_component: dict[int, int],
+    recipe: dict[str, Any],
+) -> dict[str, list[list[WeightedRidge]]]:
+    """Stream component groups into the three non-held-out fold models."""
+    model_config = recipe["model"]
+    alpha = float(model_config["ridge_alpha"])
+    stride = int(model_config["fit_row_stride"])
+    fold_count = int(recipe["cv"]["fold_count"])
+    widths = {arm: int(recipe["features"]["arms"][arm]["width"]) for arm in ARMS}
+    stats = {
+        arm: [[WeightedStats.empty(int(widths[arm])) for _ in range(2)] for _ in range(fold_count)]
+        for arm in ARMS
+    }
+    trained_components = {fold: 0 for fold in range(fold_count)}
+    clip_value = float(model_config["target_clip"])
+    first_sequence: np.ndarray | None = None
+    first_outputs: dict[str, np.ndarray] | None = None
+    reset_checked = False
+
+    for position, member in enumerate(members, start=1):
+        component = member["component"]
+        heldout_fold = fold_by_component[component]
+        sequence = source.read(member["row_group"], targets=True, mask=False)
+        if sequence.seq_ix != member["seq_ix"] or sequence.targets is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"fit sequence identity/targets mismatch at {member['row_group']}")
+        if sequence.features.shape[0] != SEQUENCE_LENGTH:
+            raise ValueError("fit sequence does not have the expected complete length")
+
+        designs = _feature_arms(sequence.features)
+        if position == 1:
+            _verify_prefix_invariants(sequence.features, designs)
+            first_sequence = sequence.features.copy()
+            first_outputs = {arm: value.copy() for arm, value in designs.items()}
+        elif position == 2:
+            if first_sequence is None or first_outputs is None:
+                raise RuntimeError("A-B-A reset check has no stored first sequence")
+            after_b = _feature_arms(first_sequence)
+            if any(not np.array_equal(first_outputs[arm], after_b[arm]) for arm in ARMS):
+                raise AssertionError("A-B-A sequence-local reset check failed")
+            reset_checked = True
+            first_sequence = None
+            first_outputs = None
+        sampled_targets = np.clip(sequence.targets[WARMUP::stride], -clip_value, clip_value).astype(
+            np.float64, copy=False
+        )

+            raise ValueError("input feature and target rows are misaligned")

+        for fold in range(fold_count):
+            if fold == heldout_fold:

+            for arm in ARMS:
+                sampled_design = designs[arm][::stride].astype(np.float64, copy=False)
+                if not np.isfinite(sampled_design).all() or not np.isfinite(sampled_targets).all():
+                    raise ValueError(f"non-finite fit values in component {component}")
+                for target_index in range(2):
+                    target = sampled_targets[:, target_index]
+                    stats[arm][fold][target_index].update(
+                        sampled_design,
+                        target,
+                        np.abs(target),
+                    )

+            json.dumps(
+                {
+                    "phase": "fit_group_complete",
+                    "position": position,
+                    "component": component,
+                    "heldout_fold": heldout_fold,
+                }
+            ),
+            flush=True,
+        )
+        del sequence, designs, sampled_targets
+
+    expected_fit_components = len(members) - int(recipe["cv"]["components_per_fold"])
+    if any(count != expected_fit_components for count in trained_components.values()):

+    if not reset_checked:

+
+    models: dict[str, list[list[WeightedRidge]]] = {}
+    for arm in ARMS:
+        models[arm] = []
+        for fold in range(fold_count):
+            target_models = [
+                WeightedRidge.fit(stats[arm][fold][target_index], alpha)
+                for target_index in range(2)
+            ]

+
+def _predict_oof(
+    source: SequenceFile,
+    members: list[dict[str, int]],
+    fold_by_component: dict[int, int],
+    models: dict[str, list[list[WeightedRidge]]],

+    row_count = SEQUENCE_LENGTH - WARMUP
+    predictions = {arm: np.empty((len(members), row_count, 2), dtype=np.float32) for arm in ARMS}
+    for position, member in enumerate(members):
+        sequence = source.read(member["row_group"], targets=False, mask=False)
+        if sequence.seq_ix != member["seq_ix"]:
+            raise ValueError(f"prediction sequence identity mismatch at {member['row_group']}")
+        designs = _feature_arms(sequence.features)
+        fold = fold_by_component[member["component"]]
+        for arm in ARMS:
+            for target_index in range(2):
+                predictions[arm][position, :, target_index] = models[arm][fold][
+                    target_index
+                ].predict(designs[arm])
+        print(
+            json.dumps(
+                {
+                    "phase": "label_blind_oof_prediction_complete",
+                    "position": position + 1,
+                    "component": member["component"],
+                    "fold": fold,
+                }
+            ),
+            flush=True,
+        )
+        del sequence, designs
+    if any(not np.isfinite(value).all() for value in predictions.values()):
+        raise FloatingPointError("OOF prediction arrays contain non-finite values")
+    return predictions
+
+
+def run(root: Path, recipe_path: Path, output_path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Run source-pinned 4-fold fitting and label-blind prediction generation."""
+    started = time.perf_counter()
+    output = require_physical_scratch(output_path)
+    if output.exists():
+        raise FileExistsError(f"refusing to overwrite existing artifacts: {output}")
+    output.mkdir(parents=True)
+
+    recipe_bytes = recipe_path.read_bytes()
+    recipe = json.loads(recipe_bytes)
+    source_hashes = verify_recipe_sources(root, recipe)
+    members, fold_by_component, input_hashes = load_members_and_folds(root, recipe)
+    selection = recipe["selection"]
+    train_path = root / selection["data_path"]
+    train_identity = verify_train_footer(train_path, selection["data_identity"])

+    # Parquet metadata is opened only after the measured footer identity passes.
+    source = SequenceFile(train_path)

+    predictions = _predict_oof(source, members, fold_by_component, models)
+
+    model_arrays: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
+    for arm in ARMS:
+        for fold, target_models in enumerate(models[arm]):
+            for target_index, model in enumerate(target_models):
+                prefix = f"{arm}_fold{fold}_target{target_index}"
+                model_arrays[f"{prefix}_mean_x"] = model.mean_x
+                model_arrays[f"{prefix}_scale_x"] = model.scale_x
+                model_arrays[f"{prefix}_coefficients"] = model.coefficients
+                model_arrays[f"{prefix}_intercept"] = np.asarray(model.intercept)
+    model_path = output / "crossfit_models.npz"
+    with model_path.open("xb") as destination:
+        np.savez(destination, **model_arrays)
+
+    prediction_paths: dict[str, str] = {}
+    prediction_hashes: dict[str, str] = {}
+    for arm, values in predictions.items():
+        path = output / f"predictions_{arm}.npy"
+        with path.open("xb") as destination:
+            np.save(destination, values, allow_pickle=False)
+        prediction_paths[arm] = str(path)
+        prediction_hashes[arm] = sha256_file(path)
+
+    member_rows = [{**member, "fold": fold_by_component[member["component"]]} for member in members]
+    members_path = output / "members.json"
+    write_json(members_path, {"members": member_rows})
+    receipt = {
+        "id": recipe["experiment_id"],
+        "phase": "crossfit_fit_and_label_blind_prediction_complete",
+        "status": "completed",
+        "recipe_sha256": _sha256_bytes(recipe_bytes),
+        "source_hashes": source_hashes,
+        "sample_source_hashes": input_hashes,
+        "data_identity": train_identity,
+        "members": member_rows,
+        "component_count": len(members),
+        "fold_count": int(recipe["cv"]["fold_count"]),
+        "components_per_fold": int(recipe["cv"]["components_per_fold"]),
+        "fit_components_per_model": len(members) - int(recipe["cv"]["components_per_fold"]),
+        "fit_rows_per_component_per_target": int(
+            np.ceil((SEQUENCE_LENGTH - WARMUP) / int(recipe["model"]["fit_row_stride"]))
+        ),
+        "target_alignment": "same input row x[t] to target y[t], after the 99-row warmup",
+        "labels_read": "fit groups only; each held-out component is excluded from its own fold model",
+        "masks_read": False,
+        "oof_prediction_reads_targets_or_masks": False,
+        "prediction_paths": prediction_paths,
+        "prediction_sha256": prediction_hashes,
+        "model_archive": str(model_path),
+        "model_archive_sha256": sha256_file(model_path),
+        "members_path": str(members_path),
+        "members_sha256": sha256_file(members_path),
+        "environment": {

+            "numpy": np.__version__,
+            "pyarrow": pyarrow.__version__,
+        },
+        "elapsed_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started,
+        "process_peak_rss_kib": resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss,
+        "gpu_used": False,
+        "official_metric": None,
+        "result_claim": None,

+    receipt_path = output / "fit_predict_receipt.json"
+    write_json(receipt_path, receipt)

+
+
+def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
+    """Parse bounded paths for the frozen experiment."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)

+    arguments = parse_args()

+"""Pinned-source and resource-safe helpers for the innovation incrementality screen."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+import numpy as np
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
+SCRATCH_ROOT = Path("/home/vlad/development/wunder/research_tmp").resolve()
+
+
+def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
+    """Hash a file incrementally, including large immutable sources."""
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as source:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: source.read(1 << 20), b""):
+            digest.update(chunk)
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+
+
+def write_json(path: Path, value: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Write one small JSON receipt atomically without replacing prior output."""
+    temporary = path.with_name(f".{path.name}.pending")
+    temporary.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n")
+    temporary.replace(path)
+
+
+def verify_recipe_sources(root: Path, recipe: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Verify all Python and metric/data implementation files before use."""
+    expected = recipe["source_hashes"]
+    observed = {str(name): sha256_file(root / str(name)) for name in expected}
+    if observed != expected:
+        raise ValueError("experiment source hashes differ from the frozen recipe")
+    return observed
+
+
+def verify_train_footer(path: Path, expected: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Check file identity and hash the pinned Parquet footer before PyArrow opens it."""
+    before = path.stat()
+    if before.st_size != int(expected["bytes"]) or before.st_mtime_ns != int(expected["mtime_ns"]):
+        raise ValueError("train Parquet size/mtime differs from the pinned source")
+
+    footer_bytes = int(expected["footer_bytes"])
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as source:
+        source.seek(-8, 2)
+        trailer = source.read(8)
+        if trailer[4:] != b"PAR1" or int.from_bytes(trailer[:4], "little") != footer_bytes:
+            raise ValueError("train Parquet trailer differs from the pinned source")
+        source.seek(-(footer_bytes + 8), 2)
+        remaining = footer_bytes + 8
+        while remaining:
+            chunk = source.read(min(1 << 20, remaining))
+            if not chunk:
+                raise ValueError("train Parquet footer ended before the pinned range")
+            digest.update(chunk)
+            remaining -= len(chunk)
+
+    after = path.stat()
+    observed = {
+        "bytes": before.st_size,
+        "mtime_ns": before.st_mtime_ns,
+        "footer_bytes": footer_bytes,
+        "footer_sha256": digest.hexdigest(),
+    }
+    if (after.st_size, after.st_mtime_ns) != (before.st_size, before.st_mtime_ns):
+        raise RuntimeError("train Parquet changed while its footer was checked")
+    if observed != expected:
+        raise ValueError("train Parquet footer hash differs from the pinned source")
+    return observed
+
+
+def load_members_and_folds(
+    root: Path, recipe: dict[str, Any]
+) -> tuple[list[dict[str, int]], dict[int, int], dict[str, str]]:
+    """Load the exact 32-sequence sample and create four component folds."""
+    selection = recipe["selection"]
+    sample_source = selection["sample_source"]
+    receipt_path = root / sample_source["path"]
+    if sha256_file(receipt_path) != sample_source["sha256"]:
+        raise ValueError("source feature-only receipt hash differs from the frozen recipe")
+    sample_receipt = json.loads(receipt_path.read_text())
+    members = [
+        {key: int(item[key]) for key in ("component", "row_group", "seq_ix")}
+        for item in sample_receipt["sample"]
+    ]
+    if len(members) != int(recipe["cv"]["component_count"]):
+        raise ValueError("sample source has an unexpected component count")
+    if len({item["component"] for item in members}) != len(members):
+        raise ValueError("component sample contains duplicates")
+
+    split_path = root / selection["split_path"]
+    split_bytes = split_path.read_bytes()
+    split_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(split_bytes).hexdigest()
+    if split_sha256 != selection["split_sha256"]:
+        raise ValueError("source-qualified split hash differs from the frozen recipe")
+    split = json.loads(split_bytes)
+    fit_groups = set(map(int, split["fit"]["train"]))
+    by_row_group = {int(record["row_group"]): record for record in split["sequences"]["train"]}
+    for member in members:
+        group = member["row_group"]
+        record = by_row_group.get(group)
+        if group not in fit_groups or record is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"sample row group {group} is outside fold0.fit.train")
+        if any(int(record[key]) != member[key] for key in ("component", "seq_ix")):
+            raise ValueError(f"sample identity changed for row group {group}")
+
+    ordered_components = np.asarray(sorted(item["component"] for item in members))
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(int(recipe["cv"]["fold_seed"]))
+    shuffled = rng.permutation(ordered_components)
+    fold_count = int(recipe["cv"]["fold_count"])
+    fold_by_component = {
+        int(component): fold
+        for fold, chunk in enumerate(np.array_split(shuffled, fold_count))
+        for component in chunk
+    }
+    expected_size = int(recipe["cv"]["components_per_fold"])
+    if any(
+        sum(value == fold for value in fold_by_component.values()) != expected_size
+        for fold in range(fold_count)
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("component folds do not match the frozen balanced design")
+
+    return (
+        members,
+        fold_by_component,
+        {
+            "sample_receipt_sha256": str(sample_source["sha256"]),
+            "split_sha256": split_sha256,
+        },
+    )
+
+
+def require_physical_scratch(path: Path) -> Path:
+    """Resolve an output path and keep it on the approved physical scratch volume."""
+    resolved = path.resolve()
+    if not resolved.is_relative_to(SCRATCH_ROOT):
+        raise ValueError(f"outputs must remain under physical scratch: {SCRATCH_ROOT}")
+    return resolved

+# Fresh-context scout: online feature and model-transfer hypotheses
+
+Created 2026-10-18 (UTC). This is a source-grounded proposal packet, not an experiment result. The first-proposal receipt records hashes before any competing campaign proposals or current actor path were inspected. I read only the assigned skills, the current online-features contract and data audit, general source indexes, primary sources/code listed in sources.json, and the recorded random library passage. No data payload, predictions, checkpoint, model code, or other agent proposal was read. No fit or implementation was run.
+
+## Contract applied
+
+The callback receives seq_ix, step_in_seq, need_prediction, and 112 current feature values. It sees neither targets nor evaluator masks. It processes every row in sequence order, including warmup steps 0–98; it predicts from step 99 onward; state resets at every sequence boundary; each answer may depend only on the current and earlier inputs from that same sequence. The 2 targets are anonymous future-movement indicators. Keep the official global_wp_clip2_v1 objective and its fixed prediction/scored masks, ±2 clipping, and original clipped-label magnitude weights unchanged in offline training and evaluation. Never use test labels, masks, future rows, sequence IDs as ordering signals, or state carried from a different sequence.
+
+The audit identifies one known component-clean F0 reference, but its evaluation panel is repeatedly exposed. All four folds have prior exposure; any follow-up needs clean source-qualified fit, teacher, initializer and component ancestry and must be described as exposed robustness evidence. The eventual scientific comparison follows the project’s paired fold/seed protocol; a cheap screen is only a screen. Current local limits are 2 aggregate CPU cores, one GPU worker with 5 GB observed VRAM and 5 GB task RAM, physical scratch at /home/vlad/development/wunder/research_tmp, no new paid compute and no B300 execution in this assignment. Final serving remains 1 CPU, 60 minutes, 20 MB. Larger teacher work is a proposal/handoff only.
+
+The participant reports supplied in the task are unverified leads, not evidence of Challenge 2 score or transfer. The six cards below are distinct mechanism families, not a requirement to run all six in one wave. The first two are intentionally cheap, input-only mechanisms; the last two ask whether training-time representation/temporal priors transfer to a compact recurrent endpoint.
+
+## P1 — Warmup-fingerprint gate over fixed experts
+**Lens:** factor the case space; change the search unit from a whole model to a sequence-level routing rule. **Family:** conditional ensemble allocation.
+
+**Source component and analogy.** Jacobs et al.’s supervised mixture of local experts uses an input-dependent gate to allocate cases among specialist predictors. The historical experiment learns subdivisions on vowel-recognition labels; it does not establish a time-series or competition gain. The randomly selected VPIN passage below is a weak analogy for conservative allocation under uncertain specialists, not evidence about these anonymous targets or the official symmetric clipped-error objective.
+
+**Intervention.** If at least two eligible source-qualified endpoints have cached predictions, fit a tiny sequence-level gate from summaries of only warmup rows 0–98 (for example, robust center/scale and a few channel-family summaries) to a small set of expert weights. Train its signal only from training-sequence out-of-fold expert predictions and training labels/masks scored by the official metric. Use strong shrinkage toward the predeclared fixed blend and constrain weights to a simplex. At test, compute the gate once from those 99 observable rows, hold its weights fixed for that sequence, and reset at the next seq_ix. The gate must never read that test sequence’s target errors or evaluator mask.
+
+**Assumptions and prediction.** There are stable, observable input-profile differences between sequences and the existing experts have different conditional error profiles. If so, the held-out component score of the gated blend should exceed its matched fixed blend while gate weights vary reproducibly with warmup fingerprints. The gate can instead overfit noisy per-sequence losses; shrinkage is central to the hypothesis.
+
+**Cheapest informative test.** On cached OOF predictions from eligible fit-only experts, fit only a low-capacity ridge/softmax gate, then score it against the same fixed blend on an outer component-excluded panel. Report pooled official WP and fold/seed exposure; use per-sequence expert errors only as evaluator diagnostics. If there are not multiple eligible experts with clean OOF predictions, do not fabricate this comparison.
+
+**Falsifier.** The gate does not beat the matched fixed blend across clean paired cells, or its expert weights are unstable across folds/seeds and do not predict conditional expert usefulness. One noisy exposed panel is a screen, not universal evidence against conditional ensembles.
+
+**Cost and artifact.** Very low inference cost: one small gate call per sequence after warmup, with no per-row gate overhead; likely a few KB plus gate-training metadata. Preserve the gate-fit sequence manifest, OOF prediction ancestry, frozen coefficients, fixed-blend comparator and evaluator receipt.
+
+## P2 — Input-only innovation clock (unconventional cheap heuristic)
+**Lens:** instrument hidden regime changes; change time from ordinal position to causal surprise. **Family:** online feature state / change detection.
+
+**Source component and analogy.** Adams and MacKay’s Bayesian online change-point detector maintains a posterior over current run length from sequential observation likelihoods and a hazard model. Its feedback is the observed input stream, not task labels. Here only the run-length/surprise idea transfers; there is no basis for inferring market events or an exchange clock from the anonymous channels.
+
+**Intervention.** Add one deterministic, target-free scalar state to the causal feature stream. Maintain reset-on-sequence diagonal fast/slow predictors for the 112 inputs; at row t compute a bounded standardized innovation summary from x_t versus statistics learned from rows before t, update a cheap CUSUM or small truncated run-length score, and append that scalar to the predictor input. Use no full covariance inverse and no target-dependent online update. Fit the supervised endpoint with this same causal statistic and official training objective. This tests a transition/surprise clock, not another fixed set of rolling w3/w13/w21 means.
+
+**Assumptions and prediction.** Some errors may arise when the observed feature process changes faster than the static recurrent state can track. If the innovation clock helps, held-out official WP should improve in a predeclared late/transition subset without degrading pooled WP, and the scalar should be causal and reset correctly.
+
+**Cheapest informative test.** First generate the scalar on bounded cached feature streams, check prefix/future-perturbation invariance and reset behavior, and inspect its distribution against step position. Then do one matched small supervised endpoint screen if the trace is nondegenerate. Keep all target/mask access inside the offline fit/evaluator.
+
+**Falsifier.** The feature-only statistic is nearly constant, mainly encodes step position, violates causal/reset invariants, or a matched endpoint shows no stable official-WP benefit. No target-free unsupervised statistic is itself evidence of a quality gain.
+
+**Cost and artifact.** O(112) scalar arithmetic and O(112) state per row, constant-size serving state and one added input; must still be profiled in the actual callback. Save the exact recurrence, numerical bounds, seed/config, invariance receipt and matched endpoint.
+
+## P3 — Cross-fitted residual head on top of a frozen recurrent endpoint
+**Lens:** re-encode the prediction as baseline plus a small correction; invert the question from “build another full model” to “is the baseline’s residual predictable?” **Family:** residual correction / conditional bias reduction.
+
+**Source component and analogy.** N-BEATS’ doubly residual stack feeds a backcast residual to later blocks and sums partial forecasts. Its paper trains point forecasts on M3/M4/Tourism-type series; its result does not transfer automatically to multivariate anonymous indicators or this metric. The proposal borrows only staged residual modeling, not the full N-BEATS architecture or its code (the ServiceNow repository is marked CC BY-NC).
+
+**Intervention.** Freeze an eligible base GRU and train a low-capacity two-target correction head on causal current-row and lag-difference features. Train against base errors generated out of fold for the sequences used to fit the head, so the head does not learn the parent’s in-sample optimism. Optimize the final combined prediction with the unchanged official objective; apply clipping only in the official metric path. Keep the head sparse/small enough to fit the package and measured runtime budget.
+
+**Assumptions and prediction.** Baseline residuals have a repeatable feature-conditional component beyond the recurrent representation. Improvement should appear in matched component-excluded pooled WP and survive fold/seed variation; the correction’s contribution should be small and interpretable enough to audit.
+
+**Cheapest informative test.** Use cached out-of-fold base predictions and a ridge correction on a predeclared compact feature set; compare base and base-plus-head on the same outer component panel. Do not compute correction targets from in-sample base predictions or tune features from evaluation labels.
+
+**Falsifier.** The correction’s apparent gain disappears with OOF parent predictions, or the correction adds unstable tail error / misses package or serving limits. In-sample residual fit alone is not a successful screen.
+
+**Cost and artifact.** One small fit and O(K) arithmetic per row for K compact inputs; likely low parameter and package cost but actual callback runtime is mandatory. Preserve OOF prediction lineage, correction features, fit manifest, output clipping path and matched score receipt.
+
+## P4 — Fit-only masked input pretraining for the eventual causal GRU
+**Lens:** relax the supervised-label bottleneck; transfer a representation objective from masked time-series modeling. **Family:** self-supervised representation pretraining.
+
+**Source component and analogy.** SimMTM learns from masked input reconstruction and uses relations among multiple masked views to reconstruct time-series structure. Its reported feedback is input reconstruction during pretraining, followed by forecasting/classification fine-tuning and evaluation; it does not report this competition’s weighted indicator metric. The official code is available, but this proposal transfers the objective idea only.
+
+**Intervention.** Pretrain a small causal GRU encoder on permitted fit-group feature rows only. For each supervised endpoint t, expose no rows later than t; mask selected current/past input entries and reconstruct only the masked input values, then discard the reconstruction decoder and fine-tune the same encoder on the official target loss. Do not include evaluation sequences in pretraining, and do not add a retrieval store or cross-sequence test-time memory. This is a causal adaptation of the reconstruction task, not a reproduction of SimMTM’s full multiview implementation.
+
+**Assumptions and prediction.** Input dynamics contain reusable structure that supervised labels alone do not reveal, and the reconstruction-trained encoder retains task-relevant information rather than spending capacity on irrelevant channel detail. Improvement should be visible in a matched student endpoint at comparable supervised updates, not merely in lower reconstruction loss.
+
+**Cheapest informative test.** On one source-qualified fit recipe, compare supervised-only initialization with fit-only causal masked pretraining followed by the same fine-tuning budget. Keep masks, epochs, seed and total update budget declared; then grade on an exposed component panel with an independent evaluator. Treat it as a fidelity/feasibility screen until the prescribed paired-cell comparison is complete.
+
+**Falsifier.** Reconstruction quality improves while official WP does not, or pretraining loses the relevant temporal variation / exceeds fit or memory budget. A cross-domain pretraining gain in the paper is not a local prior.
+
+**Cost and artifact.** Medium-to-high GPU training cost and careful group exclusion; no inference cost if the decoder is discarded, and the final GRU should retain its serving envelope. Preserve pretraining membership, masks, objective, encoder SHA, fine-tune ancestry and separate pretraining/quality results.
+
+## P5 — Chrono gate-bias initialization as a fixed-budget GRU arm
+**Lens:** change the time representation before learning. **Family:** recurrent timescale prior.
+
+**Source component and analogy.** Tallec and Ollivier derive gate-bias initialization for LSTMs/GRUs from a distribution of temporal scales; their paper studies sequence prediction and long-delay/warping tasks, not the anonymous Challenge 2 labels. This suggests an initialization ablation where sequence lengths may expose temporal dependencies at varied scales, but the maximum 20,000-step length is not evidence that useful target memory is 20,000 steps.
+
+**Intervention.** On the canonical GRU component, initialize update/retention gate biases to a predeclared spread of timescales, deriving the sign and gate convention from the actual cell semantics. Hold parameter count, data membership, optimizer, update order, clipping, loss and budget fixed. Do not add parameters, features or inference branches.
+
+**Assumptions and prediction.** The current gate initialization may make useful time constants hard to learn under the admitted training horizon. A positive result should improve the official validation trajectory or final WP across matched seeds without changing serving cost; faster early loss alone is not sufficient.
+
+**Cheapest informative test.** Fit one matched pair with identical source-qualified data and seed/update budget, standard versus chrono bias only. Check gate initialization numerically and compare the same evaluator outputs; later promotion requires the paired fold/seed protocol. Community code exists, but no author-maintained reference implementation was verified for this scout; use the paper equations and project cell semantics, not copied code.
+
+**Falsifier.** No stable quality effect after equal training budget, or the selected time-scale range pushes gates into saturation / hurts adaptation. One negative initialization is not a universal rejection of all recurrent time-scale priors.
+
+**Cost and artifact.** One standard-size GRU fit, zero extra inference cost or package parameters. Preserve exact gate-bias vector, model factory/source SHA, initialization checks and paired training/evaluation receipt.
+
+## P6 — Larger causal-window teacher distilled into the competition GRU
+**Lens:** transfer capacity, then change the search unit to a serving-sized student. **Family:** heterogeneous teacher-to-student transfer.
+
+**Source component and analogy.** TimeKD provides a time-series teacher/student distillation framework with prediction/feature transfer, but its teacher explicitly uses future ground-truth prompts as privileged input. That part is unavailable here and must not be copied. The only proposed transfer is offline distillation from teacher outputs computed on legal causal input windows into a compact GRU.
+
+**Intervention.** For each labeled fit row t, build a teacher input from x[max(0,t−59):t], ending at t. A larger window Transformer or bidirectional recurrent teacher may be bidirectional within this fully observed trailing window; it must not read x[t+1:] or teacher labels at inference. Train its endpoint predictions with the same official training objective, then stream its predictions (and optionally aligned hidden summaries) as soft targets while training the existing GRU student on hard labels plus a predeclared prediction-distillation term. Keep evaluation data excluded from teacher, student initializer and teacher cache. A student-only fit with matched updates is the control.
+
+**Assumptions and prediction.** A wider model can use cross-channel and 60-step context to produce smoother, more informative training targets, and the GRU can compress that signal without serving teacher cost. The prediction is student WP improvement versus matched student-only training, plus teacher WP as a diagnostic; a strong teacher alone is not the competition deliverable.
+
+**Cheapest informative test.** First verify a causal-window materializer on tiny synthetic prefixes and future-perturbation tests. Then one bounded teacher/student feasibility arm and a matched student-only control, with streaming teacher targets rather than a full 250-million-row cache. Run B300 only under a separately assigned, already-authorized operator; this scout did not access or execute B300. Apply clean ancestry and the full paired comparison before making a recipe claim.
+
+**Falsifier.** Teacher has no clean-component advantage, teacher outputs are too noisy or redundant to help, or the student does not exceed the same-budget control. Any teacher that uses future input rows, test labels, is_scored, or cross-sequence adaptation is invalid regardless of score.
+
+**Cost and artifact.** Highest compute cost; B300 training is an unexecuted future handoff, not admitted by this task. The deployed artifact remains a GRU under 20 MB and must pass the 1-CPU/60-minute callback profile. Preserve teacher architecture, causal window code/spec, source/fit ancestry, teacher checkpoint, streamed target manifest, student objective and measured student runtime.
+
+## Triage of the supplied reports
+
+| Report | ABI-aware assessment |
+|---|---|
+| Rolling windows w3/w13/w21 | Causal if each window ends at the current row and warmup is processed consistently. They are a low novelty baseline; only test predeclared windows with a matched endpoint and runtime measurement. |
+| Highway head / two-stage residual GRU or LSTM boosting | The useful bounded form is P3’s small correction trained on cross-fitted parent predictions. A second full recurrent model is a different, more expensive arm and needs its own matched endpoint. |
+| Late-checkpoint SWA | Source-supported as an optimization hypothesis, but only average checkpoints from the same architecture and one connected training trajectory. Do not average unrelated seeds/parents. If a compatible trajectory already exists, a same-run average versus final checkpoint is a cheap screen; availability was not checked. |
+| Variance augmentation | Fit-side only. A forecasting paper studies GRATIS, moving-block bootstrap and DTW barycenter augmentation for global RNNs on forecasting datasets; this is not evidence that independent channel scaling/noise preserves anonymous-channel relations here. A future screen should preserve sequence/channel structure, train only on fit groups, and measure the unchanged metric. |
+| Chrono initialization | P5 is the concrete matched test; no transfer gain is assumed. |
+| Causal last-60 bidirectional teacher | P6 preserves causality by ending every bidirectional teacher window at the current t. A window that contains later test rows is forbidden. |
+| Adaptive sequence weights from sequence errors | At test this is unavailable and prohibited. P1 replaces it with a training-fitted gate using OOF training errors and test-time observable warmup features only. |
+| Masked autoreconstruction | P4 limits it to fit-group inputs and a causal encoder objective; test sequences never enter pretraining. |
+| GRU future-input extractor feeding a Transformer | Future inputs are not available at prediction time. A teacher may use channel interactions over the trailing observed window, but no future input stream. |
+
+## Allocation note
+
+No numerical priors are assigned. The high-information first look is to check whether clean, cached multi-expert OOF predictions exist for P1 and to materialize/verify the one-scalar P2 statistic. P3 is the next low-cost supervised screen if a clean OOF base exists. P4–P6 are higher-cost lineages and should not delay a runnable leading endpoint. All reported fold results remain exposed; no score is predicted from public feedback. The research controller owns allocation, admission, implementation and grading.

+# All-channel causal innovation clock
+
+## Question
+
+Can a small diagonal Kalman filter over the 112 raw inputs produce a useful
+sequence-local change clock for a recurrent model? This first screen only
+checks that the feature is causal, stable and nondegenerate in fit-side data.
+It does not fit an endpoint or score a target.
+
+## Frozen recipe
+
+[recipe.json](recipe.json) fixes a 32-component sample drawn only from
+`fold0.fit.train`, one complete sequence per component. It centers and scales
+each channel from the first 99 observed rows, computes pre-update standardized
+innovations with fixed diagonal `Q=0.001`, `R=1.0`, averages clipped squared
+innovation across channels, and updates a bounded CUSUM. The candidate scalar
+is `log1p(CUSUM)`; original input channels remain intact. All estimator state
+resets at sequence boundaries. The feature reader requests only `seq_ix` and
+the 112 raw input columns.
+
+The source footer and split hashes are checked before opening Parquet metadata.
+The measured 1.5 GB reservation comes from the successful metadata-only and
+one-row-group source-reader profiles in the [source audit](../../../unified/operations/P2_INNOVATION_CLOCK_SOURCE_AUDIT_20261018_R1.md)
+and [runtime profile records](../causal_label_proxy_r1/profile_receipt_r1.json).
+The old 1.0 GB unbounded metadata attempt remains a separate incident and is
+not repeated.
+
+## Results
+
+The bounded pass completed on 32 fit-side components / 640,000 input rows.
+Average component-level innovation RMS rose from 1.792 at rows 99-499 to
+2.635 at rows 10,000-19,999. Innovation distributions differed consistently
+by semantic group: `i1_ask_price_like` was highest through later bins and
+`i0_trade_price` remained among the lowest. The scalar CUSUM's median
+component 95th percentile reached its `log(21)` cap by rows 500-2,000; its
+upper tail loses resolution, while component and time variation remain.
+
+This is a feature-distribution result with no target association or endpoint
+score. It may reflect warmup-scale mismatch, later volatility changes, or
+sequence-specific regimes. The next representation to screen is a group-aware
+fast/slow innovation vector that preserves differences between the 13 semantic
+channel groups. An independent [Data Sentinel review](../../../../unified/reviews/INNOVATION_CLOCK_FEATURE_SCREEN_REVIEW_20261018_R1.md)
+confirmed source membership, input-only projection, causality/reset checks,
+resource receipt and summary hashes. It found a wording issue in the original
+machine result's top/bottom group labels; the
+[correction addendum](review_correction_r1.json) preserves the per-bin result
+without rewriting the original artifact. The [result](result_r1.json) and
+copied [feature-only receipt](feature_only_receipt_r1.json) preserve measured
+values and provenance; detailed tables stay on physical scratch. No submission
+or new B300 draft follows from this diagnostic. Broader causal-innovation and
+Kalman teacher/student directions already exist in draft PRs #14 and #17.
+
+## Source records
+
+The screen implementation is split into [innovation_features.py](innovation_features.py)
+and [screen.py](screen.py). It is registered as
+`H-ONLINE-INNOVATION-CLOCK-20261018-R1` /
+`E-ONLINE-INNOVATION-CLOCK-FEATURE-20261018-R1`, descending from H-240.

+"""Small causal feature extractor for an all-channel Kalman innovation clock."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import numpy as np
+from numpy.typing import NDArray
+
+N_FEATURES = 112
+WARMUP_ROWS = 99
+PROCESS_VARIANCE = 0.001
+OBSERVATION_VARIANCE = 1.0
+CUSUM_DECAY = 0.95
+CUSUM_BASELINE = 1.0
+CUSUM_CAP = 20.0
+
+FEATURE_GROUPS: dict[str, tuple[int, int]] = {
+    "i0_bid_price_like": (0, 11),
+    "i0_ask_price_like": (11, 22),
+    "i0_bid_volume_like": (22, 33),
+    "i0_ask_volume_like": (33, 44),
+    "i0_trade_price": (44, 48),
+    "i0_trade_volume": (48, 52),
+    "i1_bid_price_like": (52, 63),
+    "i1_ask_price_like": (63, 74),
+    "i1_bid_volume_like": (74, 85),
+    "i1_ask_volume_like": (85, 96),
+    "i1_trade_price": (96, 100),
+    "i1_trade_volume": (100, 104),
+    "additional": (104, 112),
+}
+
+FloatArray = NDArray[np.float32]
+
+
+def innovation_clock(sequence: np.ndarray) -> tuple[FloatArray, FloatArray, FloatArray]:
+    """Return all-channel surprise, semantic-group surprise, and one scalar clock.
+
+    The first 99 observed rows initialize per-sequence centering/scaling. For
+    every later row, innovations are computed before the Kalman state update.
+    The returned scalar clock is suitable for appending while retaining raw
+    inputs; it is not a fitted feature or a quality claim.
+    """
+    values = np.asarray(sequence)
+    if values.ndim != 2 or values.shape[1] != N_FEATURES or not WARMUP_ROWS < len(values) <= 20_000:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"expected between {WARMUP_ROWS + 1} and 20,000 rows of {N_FEATURES} features"
+        )
+    if not np.isfinite(values).all():
+        raise ValueError("feature sequence contains non-finite values")
+
+    warmup = values[:WARMUP_ROWS].astype(np.float64, copy=False)
+    center = warmup.mean(axis=0)
+    scale = np.maximum(warmup.std(axis=0, ddof=1), 1e-6)
+    observations = (values[WARMUP_ROWS:].astype(np.float64) - center) / scale
+
+    level = np.zeros(N_FEATURES, dtype=np.float64)
+    covariance = np.ones(N_FEATURES, dtype=np.float64)
+    innovation_rms = np.empty(len(observations), dtype=np.float32)
+    group_rms = np.empty((len(observations), len(FEATURE_GROUPS)), dtype=np.float32)
+    clock = np.empty(len(observations), dtype=np.float32)
+    starts = np.fromiter((bounds[0] for bounds in FEATURE_GROUPS.values()), dtype=np.int64)
+    widths = np.fromiter(
+        (bounds[1] - bounds[0] for bounds in FEATURE_GROUPS.values()), dtype=np.float64
+    )
+    clock_state = 0.0
+
+    for row_index, observation in enumerate(observations):
+        predicted_covariance = covariance + PROCESS_VARIANCE
+        residual = observation - level
+        standardized = residual / np.sqrt(predicted_covariance + OBSERVATION_VARIANCE)
+        clipped_squared = np.square(np.clip(standardized, -8.0, 8.0))
+        channel_mean_square = clipped_squared.mean()
+        innovation_rms[row_index] = np.sqrt(channel_mean_square)
+        group_mean_square = np.add.reduceat(clipped_squared, starts) / widths
+        group_rms[row_index] = np.sqrt(group_mean_square)
+
+        clock_state = min(
+            CUSUM_CAP,
+            max(0.0, CUSUM_DECAY * clock_state + float(innovation_rms[row_index]) - CUSUM_BASELINE),
+        )
+        clock[row_index] = np.log1p(clock_state)
+
+        gain = predicted_covariance / (predicted_covariance + OBSERVATION_VARIANCE)
+        level += gain * residual
+        covariance = (1.0 - gain) * predicted_covariance
+
+    if not (
+        np.isfinite(innovation_rms).all()
+        and np.isfinite(group_rms).all()
+        and np.isfinite(clock).all()
+    ):
+        raise FloatingPointError("innovation clock produced a non-finite value")
+    return innovation_rms, group_rms, clock

+def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
+    """Hash a small pinned source file incrementally."""
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as source:
+        for chunk in iter(lambda: source.read(1 << 20), b""):
+            digest.update(chunk)
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+
+
+def verify_train_identity(path: Path) -> dict[str, int | str]:
+    """Verify immutable file metadata and footer before PyArrow opens it."""
+    stat_before = path.stat()
+    observed: dict[str, int | str] = {
+        "bytes": stat_before.st_size,
+        "mtime_ns": stat_before.st_mtime_ns,
+        "footer_bytes": EXPECTED_DATA["footer_bytes"],
+    }
+    if (
+        observed["bytes"] != EXPECTED_DATA["bytes"]
+        or observed["mtime_ns"] != EXPECTED_DATA["mtime_ns"]
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(f"train file size/mtime differs from frozen source: {observed}")
+
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as source:
+        source.seek(-8, 2)
+        trailer = source.read(8)
+        footer_bytes = int.from_bytes(trailer[:4], "little")
+        if trailer[4:] != b"PAR1" or footer_bytes != EXPECTED_DATA["footer_bytes"]:
+            raise ValueError("train Parquet footer trailer differs from the pinned identity")
+        source.seek(-(footer_bytes + 8), 2)
+        remaining = footer_bytes + 8
+        while remaining:
+            chunk = source.read(min(1 << 20, remaining))
+            if not chunk:
+                raise ValueError("train Parquet ended before the pinned footer was read")
+            digest.update(chunk)
+            remaining -= len(chunk)
+    observed["footer_sha256"] = digest.hexdigest()
+    stat_after = path.stat()
+    if (stat_after.st_size, stat_after.st_mtime_ns) != (
+        stat_before.st_size,
+        stat_before.st_mtime_ns,
+    ):
+        raise RuntimeError("train Parquet changed while its bounded footer identity was checked")
+    if observed != EXPECTED_DATA:
+        raise ValueError(f"train Parquet footer hash differs from frozen source: {observed}")
+    return observed
+
+
+def verify_sources(
+    root: Path, recipe_path: Path, split_path: Path
+) -> tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Verify the recipe's source pins and load the fixed split manifest."""
+    recipe_bytes = recipe_path.read_bytes()
+    recipe = json.loads(recipe_bytes)
+    split_bytes = split_path.read_bytes()
+    split_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(split_bytes).hexdigest()
+    if split_sha256 != EXPECTED_SPLIT_SHA256:
+        raise ValueError("fold0 split differs from the feature-only recipe")
+    source_hashes = {str(path): sha256_file(root / path) for path in recipe["source_hashes"]}
+    if source_hashes != recipe["source_hashes"]:
+        raise ValueError(f"source file hashes differ from recipe: {source_hashes}")
+    return {
+        "recipe_sha256": hashlib.sha256(recipe_bytes).hexdigest(),
+        "split_sha256": split_sha256,
+        **source_hashes,
+    }, json.loads(split_bytes)
+
+
+def choose_fit_sequences(split: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, int]]:
+    """Select one complete sequence from each of 32 fit-only components."""
+    fit_groups = set(map(int, split["fit"]["train"]))
+    by_component: dict[int, list[dict[str, int]]] = {}
+    for record in split["sequences"]["train"]:
+        group = int(record["row_group"])
+        if group in fit_groups and group != 528:
+            by_component.setdefault(int(record["component"]), []).append(record)
+    components = np.asarray(sorted(by_component), dtype=np.int64)
+    if len(components) < SAMPLE_COMPONENTS:
+        raise ValueError("fewer than 32 source-qualified fitting components are available")
+    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
+    selected_components = rng.choice(components, SAMPLE_COMPONENTS, replace=False)
+    selected: list[dict[str, int]] = []
+    for component in selected_components:
+        records = sorted(by_component[int(component)], key=lambda record: int(record["row_group"]))
+        record = records[int(rng.integers(len(records)))]
+        selected.append({key: int(record[key]) for key in ("component", "row_group", "seq_ix")})
+    return selected
+

+def summarize_bin(values: np.ndarray, row_start: int, row_end: int) -> dict[str, float | int]:
+    """Summarize one sequence-local time bin without retaining row data."""
+    start, end = row_start - WARMUP_ROWS, row_end - WARMUP_ROWS
+    if start < 0 or end > len(values) or end <= start:
+        raise ValueError(f"invalid feature bin [{row_start}, {row_end})")
+    block = values[start:end].astype(np.float64, copy=False)
+    return {
+        "row_start": row_start,
+        "row_end": row_end,
+        "mean": float(block.mean()),
+        "median": float(np.median(block)),
+        "p95": float(np.quantile(block, 0.95)),
+    }
+

+def write_csv(path: Path, rows: list[dict[str, Any]], columns: list[str]) -> None:
+    """Write a small summary table to physical scratch."""
+    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as output:
+        writer = csv.DictWriter(output, fieldnames=columns)

+        writer.writerows(rows)

+    component_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    group_rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    first_features: np.ndarray | None = None
+    first_output: tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None = None
+    first_prefix: tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None = None

+        result = innovation_clock(sequence.features)

+            first_features = sequence.features.copy()
+            first_output = tuple(value.copy() for value in result)

+        for row_start, row_end in TIME_BINS:
+            global_stats = summarize_bin(result[0], row_start, row_end)
+            clock_stats = summarize_bin(result[2], row_start, row_end)
+            component_rows.append(

+                    **member,

+                    "clock_p95": clock_stats["p95"],
+                    "clock_fraction_gt_1": float(

+# Expanded causal Kalman input replay
+
+## Question and status
+
+This follow-up tests whether the small positive local-trend input-replacement point on the original 16-group panel persists across a wider portion of the same exposed F0. The frozen panel uses the first 141 source-qualified fold-0 evaluation groups, covering 82 components. This is an exposure-aware discovery continuation, not clean validation or independent confirmation. The replay is prediction-only: no parameters are fitted, and it compares the raw parent with the same fixed local-trend posterior replacement used in the first screen.
+
+The recipe is frozen in [recipe_r1.json](recipe_r1.json). It pins the representative completed GRU replay profile and its source recipe by SHA-256; the preflight verifies the profile is successful, below the declared RAM/VRAM caps, and uses the same frozen inference path before the controller reserves resources. The replay and independent evidence review are complete. Status: **inconclusive positive, discovery only**.
+

+            digest.update(block)
+    return digest.hexdigest()

+    expected_steps = np.arange(ROWS, dtype=np.int64)

+        steps = table["step_in_seq"].to_numpy()
+        need = table["need_prediction"].to_numpy().astype(bool, copy=False)

+            mask[index : index + 1],

+def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
+    """Hash a file incrementally to keep peak memory independent of file size."""
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as stream:
+        for block in iter(lambda: stream.read(1 << 20), b""):
+            digest.update(block)
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+

+def digest_ints(values: list[int]) -> str:
+    """Hash an ordered integer list as compact JSON."""
+    payload = json.dumps(values, separators=(",", ":")).encode("ascii")
+    return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()

+        raise RuntimeError("unified cgroup membership is unavailable")
+    return Path("/sys/fs/cgroup") / unified.lstrip("/")

+    for name in names:
+        try:

+            values[name] = {"unavailable": str(error)}
+        else:

+def verify_parquet_footer(path: Path, expected: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:

+    expected_size = int(expected["footer_bytes"])

+        if trailer[4:] != b"PAR1" or footer_size != expected_size:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "parquet footer size or trailer differs from the frozen split manifest"
+            )
+        stream.seek(-(footer_size + 8), os.SEEK_END)
+        remaining = footer_size + 8
+        while remaining:
+            block = stream.read(min(remaining, 1 << 20))
+            if not block:
+                raise ValueError("valid.parquet footer is truncated")
+            digest.update(block)
+            remaining -= len(block)
+    actual = {"footer_bytes": footer_size, "footer_sha256": digest.hexdigest()}
+    if actual["footer_sha256"] != expected["footer_sha256"]:
+        raise ValueError("valid.parquet footer digest differs from the frozen split manifest")
+    return actual

+    frozen = json.loads(PREFLIGHT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    fresh = static_contract()
+    keys = (
+        "recipe_sha256",
+        "source_hashes",
+        "resource_profile",
+        "prior_preflight_sha256",
+        "split_manifest_sha256",
+        "data",
+        "parent",
+        "membership",
+        "arms",
+    )
+    if frozen.get("status") != "pass_identity_step_order_targets_masks_blind" or any(
+        frozen.get(key) != fresh[key] for key in (*keys, "identity_and_step_order")
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("frozen preflight no longer matches sources, data metadata, or membership")
+    return frozen, json.loads(OLD_PREFLIGHT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+
+
+def write_cache(
+    output_dir: Path, arm: str, values: np.ndarray, preflight: dict[str, Any]
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Atomically persist one prediction cache and its identity sidecar."""
+    cache = output_dir / f"{arm}.npy"
+    temporary = cache.with_suffix(".npy.partial")
+    with temporary.open("wb") as stream:
+        np.save(stream, np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float32), allow_pickle=False)
+        stream.flush()
+        os.fsync(stream.fileno())
+    os.replace(temporary, cache)
+    receipt = {
+        "schema": "wnn.kalman_input_panel_prediction.v1",
+        "arm": arm,
+        "cache_path": str(cache),
+        "cache_sha256": sha256_file(cache),
+        "cache_bytes": cache.stat().st_size,
+        "prediction_shape": list(values.shape),
+        "prediction_dtype": "float32",
+        "group_order_sha256": preflight["membership"]["group_order_sha256"],
+        "sequence_id_order_sha256": preflight["membership"]["sequence_id_order_sha256"],
+        "groups": preflight["membership"]["groups"],
+        "sequence_ids": preflight["membership"]["sequence_ids"],
+        "checkpoint_sha256": preflight["parent"]["checkpoint_sha256"],
+        "normalization_sha256": preflight["parent"]["normalization_sha256"],
+        "preflight_sha256": sha256_file(PREFLIGHT),
+        "source_hashes": preflight["source_hashes"],
+        "targets_or_masks_loaded": False,
+        "official_metric_called": False,
+    }
+    receipt_path = output_dir / f"{arm}.json"
+    with receipt_path.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
+        json.dump(receipt, stream, indent=2, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False)
+        stream.write("\n")
+    return receipt
+
+

+    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

+# Causal Kalman filtering of model outputs
+
+## Question and status
+
+Can a per-sequence causal local-level filter reduce noise in the frozen model's two output streams, without changing model weights or reading target labels at inference? The frozen screen completed. Both filters underperformed the raw parent on the exposed F0 panel; independent review confirmed the scoring and claim limits.
+
+## Frozen method
+
+Use the exact full-validation prediction cache for `warm_mechanism_f0_s3_c_r3`, whose checkpoint, prediction bytes, sidecar and prior fit-membership preflight are pinned in [recipe.json](recipe.json). Generate two deterministic arms:
+
+1. A steady-state scalar local-level Kalman filter with fixed `Q/R = 0.25` for both predicted target channels.
+2. The same filter with `Q/R` estimated separately per sequence/channel from the first 99 model outputs, using robust variances of first and second differences and the clipped method-of-moments equations in the recipe. The observation-variance estimate has a frozen `1e-12` floor, including for constant prefixes.
+
+The state resets for every sequence. Rows 0–98 are an unscored calibration/warmup prefix: the adaptive gain uses those 99 predictions, and filtered prefix values are not evaluated. Every scored output from row 99 onward uses the calibrated prefix and predictions only through its current row. The filter never sees labels or scoring masks. The unchanged parent prediction is the control. No model fitting is involved.
+
+Scoring uses the official `global_wp_clip2_v1` metric on 468 previously inspected F0 groups and 141 source-qualified components, excluding rows 0–98. The paired component bootstrap and four deterministic descriptive component partitions are conditional on fixed predictions; they do not provide clean-CV, seed, or public-transfer evidence.
+
+## Result
+
+| Endpoint | WP | Difference from raw parent | Paired component-bootstrap 95% CI |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|
+| Raw parent | 0.6812265 | — | — |
+| Fixed `Q/R=0.25` | 0.6755207 | −0.0057059 | [−0.0065918, −0.0050088] |
+| First-99 estimated `Q/R` | 0.6647620 | −0.0164645 | [−0.0190768, −0.0144069] |
+
+Both filters lose in all four descriptive component partitions. The preregistered strong follow-up criterion was not met. The adaptive estimate has broad, frequently clipped gains (median Q/R 0.528; median gain 0.509; 10th–90th percentile Q/R spans 0.01–4.0), which is unstable evidence for the local-level noise model. These results narrow only these two ways of smoothing the model's output stream; they do not reject Kalman-derived inputs or hidden states, learned teacher features, student transfer, or online feedback methods.
+
+## Source identity and pre-run correction
+
+The F0 group, sequence and component order digests match the frozen split and the existing parent preflight. The initial recipe draft had two malformed 64-character digest pins. Its exact bytes are preserved in [recipe_r1_initial_bad_hash_pins.json](recipe_r1_initial_bad_hash_pins.json); both errors were caught using split/recipe metadata before reading prediction arrays, target arrays or masks. Static review also caught a wrong fold-helper reference and an omitted variance floor in the recipe. Both were corrected and independently rechecked before prediction generation or target/mask scoring.
+
+## Code and next stages
+
+- [Prediction generator](generate_predictions.py) verifies the pinned full-validation source and writes only filter predictions plus a label-blind receipt under physical scratch.
+- [Grader](grade_output_filter.py) verifies prediction/output order and parent ancestry, writes [preflight_r1.json](preflight_r1.json) before target/mask numeric use, then applies the official metric and paired component bootstrap.
+- [Execution receipt](execution_receipt_r1.json) records the one-group profile, full-cache identity, scope limits, sampled memory/CPU observations and unchanged parent OOM counters. The full 149,760,128-byte prediction cache and its per-group receipt remain in `/home/vlad/development/wunder/research_tmp/online_features_r1/kalman_output_filter_r1/`; exact generation wall time was not captured.
+- [Independent evidence review](../../../../unified/reviews/KALMAN_OUTPUT_FILTER_EVIDENCE_REVIEW_20261018_R1.md) confirms score, folds, bootstrap and claim scope. It notes that the configured runtime cap is not a measured elapsed-time result.
+
+This is a fixed-model serving treatment, not a large-scale training direction. It does not warrant a new B300 draft by itself. The separate retained-raw learned Kalman feature teacher/student study remains in [draft PR #17](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/17).

+def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:

+# Recurrent interaction with groupwise Kalman states
+
+**Status: completed two-seed local screen on the same exposed F0 panel. The active-state delta changes sign across seeds and remains tiny relative to uncertainty; keep the mechanism open without promoting a stable gain.**
+
+## Question
+
+Does a GRU learn useful interactions with causal groupwise fast/slow Kalman innovation states when the same 39 appended columns are present but zeroed in the matched control? The prior four-fold ridge screen was negative for this encoding, but it did not test recurrent nonlinear interactions. This is the narrow next screen recommended by the independent research strategist.
+
+## Frozen feature definition
+
+- Preserve all112 raw input fields and existing event features.
+- Normalize each sequence's input channels using only its first99 rows (mean and sample standard deviation, floor1e-6).
+- Starting at row99, compute pre-update standardized innovations from a diagonal random-walk Kalman filter with `Q=0.001`, `R=1`, initial level0 and covariance1; clip innovations to ±8.
+- For each of13 documented semantic groups, compute mean squared innovation, then fast and slow exponential states with spans20 and200. Append `log1p(fast)`, `log1p(slow)`, and `log(fast+1e-8)-log(slow+1e-8)`, for39 features total. Rows0–98 receive zero features.
+- Every state resets at the sequence boundary. The extractor reads no labels, mask, sequence identifier or future row.
+
+The local implementation is in [`src/wnn/kalman_group_features.py`](../../../../src/wnn/kalman_group_features.py), with trainer/checkpoint integration in the other pinned source files listed by the recipe. It supports batched full-sequence training and a one-row streaming state. Full-precision feature computation follows the frozen NumPy reference; output columns are float32.
+
+## Preflight evidence
+
+The [preflight script](preflight_features.py) reads only the112 input columns for one fitting-side sequence. It compares the new feature path with the earlier frozen `group_features.py` implementation; checks NumPy, batched Torch, and one-row Torch/NumPy streaming agreement; and checks a future perturbation and reset. The [receipt](preflight_result_r1.json) records the source group, feature hash and numeric errors. It does not read labels or masks and makes no quality claim.
+
+The actual B8, 20k-row CUDA profile is recorded in [profile_receipt_r1.json](profile_receipt_r1.json). It completed60 timed loader batches (610 optimizer attempts across the chunked sequence batches), with finite losses and gradients. Peak worker RAM was4.05GB under the4.5GB cap; peak observed VRAM was1.38GB. Worker and parent OOM/max counters stayed at zero. The controller logged memory-high events near the worker threshold, so the fit pair keeps the same4.5GB hard cap and is admitted one arm at a time. The first launch request was rejected by the controller's CPU accounting before any GPU work; the successful profile used a half-core controller scope and one-core worker reservation.
+
+## Matched comparison
+
+The [recipe](recipe_r1.json) pairs an active-state fit against an equal-width all-zero feature control. Both start from `warm_mechanism_f0_s3_c_r3@ep1`, use the same32 complete source-qualified fit components, seed3, batch8, chunks2000, full FP32, one epoch, weighted MSE, AdamW/OneCycle and a fixed epoch-0 checkpoint. Parent-inherited auxiliary weights are also identical (`aux_next=0.3`, `aux_struct=0.3`). The active representation differs only in the values of the 39 appended features. All old parent columns remain present in both arms.
+
+Both fits and feature-only evaluation exports completed. Active scored0.67986413 WP versus0.67981250 for zero control (Δ+0.00005163). A paired141-component bootstrap gave a conditional 95% interval [−0.00013143,+0.00027018]. The time-bin deltas change sign, from +0.00022656 at rows99–499 to −0.00023541 at rows500–1,999, then small positive values later. See the detailed [results note](RESULTS_R1.md) and machine-readable [grade](grade_result_r1.json). This does not warrant a new B300 draft or a family-level reject. A fit-only scaling/bounding variant is the next useful local screen; existing causal-innovation and Kalman teacher/student handoffs remain in draft PRs [#14](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/14) and [#17](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/17).
+
+### Seed-4 sensitivity follow-up
+
+The frozen [seed-4 recipe](recipe_seed4_r1.json) repeats the same active-versus-zero comparison on the same fit components and F0 evaluation panel, changing only the stochastic seed. Active scored0.68037958 WP versus0.68039346 for zero control (Δ−0.00001387; conditional 141-component 95% interval [−0.00017548,+0.00012404]). Across seeds3 and4, the paired deltas are +0.00005163 and −0.00001387; their arithmetic mean +0.00001888 is descriptive, not a training-variability estimate. The feature effect is small and sign-unstable on this panel. The detailed [seed-4 result](RESULTS_SEED4_R1.md), [hash-bound prediction freeze](prediction_freeze_seed4_r1.json), [machine grade](grade_result_seed4_r1.json), and [execution/failure receipt](execution_receipt_seed4_r1.json) preserve the values and provenance. The first grade attempt failed after scoring because it expected absent `score.json` files; the same frozen pair then graded successfully with no score-dependent model change. This follow-up still does not reject the family or establish a robust benefit.
+
+Fixed additive group states and fixed output smoothing are weak mechanisms on the measured screens. A separate literature-grounded direction is now being drafted: learn a causal, innovation-conditioned latent update/gain inside the recurrent teacher, keep raw inputs intact, and test teacher-to-student transfer. This changes the state-update mechanism and is not a new claim about the two local screens.

+# Recurrent groupwise Kalman-state screen R1
+
+**Status: completed local screen; tiny exposed-F0 point increase with substantial conditional uncertainty. Keep the representation family open; no new B300 draft is justified by this result alone.**
+
+## Question and exact comparison
+
+The earlier groupwise fast/slow Kalman-state weighted-ridge proxy lost against raw inputs, but did not test recurrent nonlinear use. This screen retained all raw and event inputs, appended the 39 causal groupwise states, and compared them with an identical-width all-zero state control. Both arms started from the same `warm_mechanism_f0_s3_c_r3@ep1` checkpoint, used the same 32 complete source-qualified fit components, seed3, batch8, chunk2000, one FP32 epoch, AdamW at `3e-5`, OneCycle, clip norm1, and fixed epoch0 checkpoint. The inherited auxiliary weights were identical: `aux_next=0.3`, `aux_struct=0.3`; the other auxiliary weights were zero.
+
+The subset has 102 train row groups and66 validation development groups from32 components. The outer F0 evaluation groups were excluded from fitting and the initializer. The parent itself was previously trained on the full F0 fit membership, so the paired adaptation tests only the incremental effect of exposing the new states on top of that common parent. It is not a scratch-trained teacher or a seed replication.
+
+## Feature and serving checks
+
+For each input channel, the feature extractor normalizes using only the first99 rows, then computes pre-update diagonal random-walk Kalman innovations. It emits fast and slow group innovation-energy summaries plus their log ratio for the13 input groups. No targets, masks, identifiers or future rows enter the extractor; state resets at each sequence boundary.
+
+On one complete20,000-row train sequence, all 39 states were finite. Batched Torch matched the NumPy implementation within `9.54e-7`; one-row Torch streaming matched the batch path within `9.54e-7`; NumPy streaming matched exactly. The frozen reference extractor differed by at most `1.91e-6`. A perturbation after row10,000 changed the preceding feature prefix by exactly zero, repeated reset output matched exactly, and the99-row warmup output was all zero. The [preflight receipt](preflight_result_r1.json) binds the source sequence and implementation hashes.
+
+The actual B8 CUDA profile completed60 timed loader batches and610 finite optimizer attempts across chunked sequences. Worker peak RAM was4.052 GB under a4.5 GB task cap, peak observed VRAM was1.407 GB, and OOM/max counters were zero. The cgroup recorded memory-high pressure near its configured threshold, so both fit arms were serialized under the same4.5 GB cap. Active and control fits completed in25.2 s each at3.327 GB and2.644 GB RAM peak, respectively; both had zero memory-event deltas. Prediction exports each covered all468 evaluation groups with shape `[468, 20000, 2]`, were finite and feature-only, and had matching evaluation-membership hashes. Prediction/export worker peaks were at most1.581 GB RAM and1.523 GB observed VRAM, with no OOM/max events.
+
+## Official metric results
+
+Scores use the unchanged `global_wp_clip2_v1` metric, its cached official `is_scored` mask, and the fixed F0 `need_prediction AND is_scored` evaluation groups. The two prediction arrays were frozen and hash-checked before the grade script read target or mask arrays.
+
+| Endpoint | WP | Target 0 | Target 1 |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|
+| Raw + active 39 states | 0.67986413 | 0.67234267 | 0.68738559 |
+| Matched raw + zero states | 0.67981250 | 0.67221912 | 0.68740587 |
+| Active minus control | **+0.00005163** | +0.00012355 | −0.00002028 |
+
+The paired component bootstrap resampled141 connected evaluation components over2,000 draws. Its conditional 95% interval for the WP difference is `[−0.00013143, +0.00027018]` (`p(delta<=0)=0.3125`). This describes fixed endpoints on repeatedly inspected F0; it excludes fitting-seed, fold, sample-selection and public-transfer uncertainty. It is not a significance or clean-validation claim.
+
+By scored position, active-minus-control WP deltas were:
+
+| Rows | Delta WP | Scored rows |
+|---|---:|---:|
+| 99–499 | +0.00022656 | 17,198 |
+| 500–1,999 | −0.00023541 | 62,742 |
+| 2,000–9,999 | +0.00012554 | 316,788 |
+| 10,000–19,999 | +0.00004391 | 412,135 |
+
+The pattern is mixed rather than a stable later-sequence improvement. The class deltas are also small and uneven: approximately +0.0000225, −0.0000233, −0.0000184, and +0.0002171 for classes0–3. Training traces show the input-projection gradient squared-share rising from2.97% in the zero control to15.71% with active features, while the readout remains dominant. This confirms the new input block receives gradient, not that it improves generalization. All210 chunk updates in each arm had finite gradients, but clip norm1 was active for100% of recorded steps.
+
+## Interpretation and next allocation
+
+The observed delta is positive but tiny relative to its component-level uncertainty. The four position bins change sign, and only one fitting seed, one exposed fold, and a 32-component incremental fine-tune were measured. This is not a reason to reject the nonlinear/recurrent direction, nor evidence for a B300 gain. The feature scale was not refit on the 32-component subset: newly appended columns inherited zero mean/unit scale, while the fast/slow log-ratio can reach magnitudes near10. Scaling or bounding the appended block is a concrete next local variant to screen, with fit-only statistics and an equal-width zero control.

+# Recurrent groupwise Kalman-state seed-4 sensitivity screen
+
+**Status: completed paired seed-4 screen. The active feature effect changes sign relative to seed 3 and remains much smaller than evaluation and fitting uncertainty. Keep the feature family open; this result does not support a stable gain.**
+
+## Frozen question and comparison
+
+Does the active-minus-zero effect for the same 39 causal groupwise fast/slow Kalman innovation-energy states persist under a second optimizer seed on the same exposed F0 panel? The seed-4 recipe changes only stochastic training randomness from the seed-3 pair. It retains the same `warm_mechanism_f0_s3_c_r3@ep1` parent, 32 complete source-qualified fit components, optimizer, update count, checkpoint policy, feature code, precision, and all-zero equal-width control.
+
+The fit uses 102 training row groups and 66 development groups from the same 32 components. Both models are incremental fine-tunes of a shared parent; this is not a scratch-trained teacher, independent data replication, fold replication, or public-transfer test. The original [seed-3 result](RESULTS_R1.md) and this repeat use the same repeatedly inspected F0 evaluation groups, so seed repetition does not make F0 fresh.
+
+## Prediction freeze and grade
+
+The active and zero-control prediction exports were checked as finite FP32 arrays of shape `[468, 20000, 2]`, with matching evaluation membership and pinned checkpoint, prediction, and sidecar hashes. The [prediction freeze](prediction_freeze_seed4_r1.json) was written before target or mask arrays were opened (`targets_read=false`, `masks_read=false`). The grader verifies that freeze and those hashes before loading the official cached targets/mask.
+
+The first grading worker completed the comparison calculation but failed while assembling the output receipt: this `--no-eval-during-fit` recipe has no per-run `score.json`, while the original grader tried to hash one. It wrote no result and emitted no score. The grader was repaired to identify each endpoint by its frozen checkpoint and prediction hashes, then the exact same pair was graded successfully. Both attempts were after the prediction freeze; no model or prediction was changed in response to the failed attempt. The [execution receipt](execution_receipt_seed4_r1.json) preserves both attempts and the failure diagnosis.
+
+## Official metric results
+
+Scores use unchanged `global_wp_clip2_v1`, the fixed F0 evaluation groups, cached `need_prediction AND is_scored`, and the row-99 scoring boundary.
+
+| Endpoint | WP | Target 0 | Target 1 |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|
+| Active 39 states, seed 4 | 0.68037958 | 0.67320791 | 0.68755126 |
+| Equal-width zero-state control, seed 4 | 0.68039346 | 0.67317990 | 0.68760701 |
+| Active minus control | **−0.00001387** | +0.00002801 | −0.00005575 |
+
+The paired bootstrap resampled 141 connected evaluation components over 2,000 draws. Its conditional 95% interval for the WP difference is `[−0.00017548, +0.00012404]`; `p_le_0=0.5805` is the fraction of bootstrap draws at or below zero, not a formal hypothesis-test p-value. This interval conditions on the two fixed seed-4 checkpoints and exposed F0 components; it excludes fit-seed, fold, feature-selection, and public-transfer uncertainty.
+
+Post-hoc position-bin deltas are mixed: `−0.00045064` at rows 99–499, `−0.00007294` at 500–1,999, `+0.00006737` at 2,000–9,999, and `−0.00004715` at 10,000–19,999. These bins are descriptive and not separate confirmatory tests.
+
+## Across-seed reading
+
+| Fit seed | Active WP | Zero-control WP | Paired delta | Conditional component 95% interval |
+|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| 3 | 0.67986413 | 0.67981250 | +0.00005163 | [−0.00013143, +0.00027018] |
+| 4 | 0.68037958 | 0.68039346 | −0.00001387 | [−0.00017548, +0.00012404] |
+
+The arithmetic mean of the two paired deltas is `+0.00001888 WP`; this is descriptive only. The sign flips, both intervals span zero, and absolute endpoint scores move about `0.00058 WP` between optimizer seeds while the treatment effect is at most `0.000052`. Two seeds on one exposed fold are not enough to estimate fit-seed variability reliably. This weakens the claim of a stable increment but does not reject the broader conditional/recurrent Kalman family.
+
+## Resources and provenance

Fit peaks were 2.62 GB and 2.58 GB RAM; prediction peaks were 1.58 GB and 1.46 GB RAM; grade peak was 0.58 GB. +Do not promote the 39 appended states as a proven quality improvement, and do not close the feature family from this two-seed result. The next *large* Kalman experiment should change the mechanism: learn a causal, innovation-conditioned latent update/gain inside a recurrent teacher while preserving raw inputs, then test whether its supervision transfers to matched GRU students. Direct output smoothing is a different treatment and already lost materially; fixed additive summaries have not shown stable value. The larger existing [PR #17](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/17) remains the local-trend teacher/student handoff. A separate learned-gain draft is being prepared because it changes the recurrent state-update mechanism rather than adding another fixed feature block. No B300 fit or competition score is claimed here.
