These additions do not start or reassign any team's running jobs.
 
+
+
 ## Question or claim
 
+
+
 Can a causal Transformer with a learned autoregressive output term produce a better teacher and, more importantly, a better deterministic GRU student for root Wunder Connectome Challenge 2?
 
+
+
 This is a detailed design proposal requested by the user. The eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs are user-reported planned resources; no access, topology, software stack, memory profile, throughput, fit, or score was verified for that cluster. Writing this plan does not reopen the paused local research campaign or authorize a remote launch. The user wants complete training and variation across fitting seeds and source-qualified folds, with quantization deferred until submission engineering.
 
+
+
 Latest user steering: “focus on best possible quality, we have a lot of compute.” This supersedes treating a small model or a short training budget as the preferred endpoint. The 86M model and six-epoch run remain matched references. Primary quality exploration expands to roughly 207M and 682M teachers, a 1.65B scale arm, longer/full-sequence context, 12/24/48-epoch training comparisons, and heterogeneous teacher ensembles, followed through actual GRU distillation. Section 19 defines this quality-first scope. The user has requested a research note, not an actual cluster launch in this turn.
 
+
+
 The recommendation is a numerical-input causal decoder Transformer with a small learned AR(1) readout outside the attention backbone. An auxiliary future-observation prediction objective is a separate, combinable autoregressive-learning arm. Neither a causal mask alone nor an auxiliary forecasting head should be misreported as feedback of past predictions.
 
+
+
 All hyperparameters below are proposed starting settings, not established competition optima. All runtime numbers are arithmetic scenarios, not B300 measurements.
 
+
+
 ## Mechanism and method
 
+
+
 ### 1. What is known about this task
 
+
+
 The [local data contract](../../../docs/data_overview.md) specifies 112 numerical features, 20,000 ordered rows per sequence, two future-price-related targets, and causal row-by-row prediction. Train has 10,607 sequences / 212,140,000 rows; supplied validation has 1,873 sequences / 37,460,000 rows. Actual fitting row counts depend on the frozen component-disjoint fold manifest and any permitted-data exclusions. The local reader documents corrupt train row group 528; do not silently include it or silently repair the canonical file.
 
+
+
 The first 99 rows update model state but require no prediction. All later rows require outputs, although only the hidden scoring subset contributes to the official score. Sequence IDs are identifiers, not chronological information. There is no usable target-history feed at inference.
 
+
+
 Crucially, the previous label y[t-1] describes future price movement relative to row t-1. Its value cannot be assumed observed at row t. The undisclosed target horizon also prevents inventing a label-maturation delay. Feeding y[t-1] during fitting and substituting a model output at inference would introduce unavailable information and a train/serve mismatch.
 
+
+
 The frozen official metric remains [global_wp_clip2_v1](../../../src/wnn/gmetric.py): predictions and labels clipped at ±2, original clipped-label magnitude weights, pooled scored rows, mean over the two target correlations. Training weights and training-target clipping are distinct recipe choices.
 
+
+
 ### 2. Proposed backbone
 
+
+
 | Component | 86M matched reference; larger quality variants in Section 19 |
+
 |---|---|
+
 | Numerical token | One complete 112-feature row |
+
 | Input mapping | MLP 112 → 768 → 768; fixed feature identities |
+
 | Blocks | 12 causal decoder blocks, pre-RMSNorm |
+
 | Hidden width | 768 |
+
 | Attention heads | 12 heads, head dimension 64; ordinary multi-head attention |
+
 | Feed-forward | SwiGLU, intermediate width 2048 |
+
 | Position | RoPE using actual row positions within the sequence |
+
 | Output branches | Two-value innovation proposal u[t], two-value AR gate a[t] |
+
 | Residual dropout | 0.05 initially |
+
 | Attention dropout | 0 initially; any change is recorded |
+
 | Nominal input window | Up to 4096 rows per training chunk, including left context |
+
 | Training precision | Strict FP32 reference; see the explicit precision distinction below |
+
 | Research model size | About 86M parameters including input/head overhead; implementation must count exactly |
 
+
+
 The approximate block count is 12 × (4 × 768² + 3 × 768 × 2048), about 84.9M before embeddings, readouts, and normalization parameters. This is our parameter arithmetic, not a measured model inventory.
 
+
+
 The decoder/normalization/feed-forward ingredients follow the mechanisms in [S17]. A proposed scale ladder is S: 8 layers / width 512 / SwiGLU 1536, about 28M parameters; M: 12 / 768 / 2048, about 86M; L: 16 / 1024 / 2816, about 207M. Compare them at both fixed compute and declared full training horizons. Scaling parameter count and context together cannot identify which change helped. These optional arms are not extra admitted spending.
 
+
+
 A grouped-input sibling uses separate MLPs for the supplied 13 feature groups, concatenated and projected into one temporal token. It does not expand each row into 112 temporal tokens. Column indices are identifiers, not guaranteed order-book depth; do not assume adjacent indices are adjacent price levels.
 
+
+
 Use frozen fitting-only feature-wise mean/standard-deviation normalization initially, flooring standard deviations at 1e-3. Record exact statistics and feature order. A whole-sequence mean/variance computed using rows after t would leak into an early prediction. Dynamic normalization, RevIN, robust scales, feature clipping, and hand-engineered clocks are separate representation arms. Pair candidate/control by explicitly copying the common initial backbone and input/head weights before adding the zero-initialized gate branch, so extra parameter initialization does not inadvertently change all common weights or the data-order RNG.
 
+
+
 RoPE is a starting positional mechanism [S1]. A row index represents event order, not physical elapsed time. Any additional clock or age feature must come from observables available at that row.
 
+
+
 ### 3. Add the autoregressive term without serializing the Transformer
 
+
+
 For each target independently, compute from the causal Transformer representation:
 
+
+
 $$
+
 u_t = g_u(H_t), \qquad
+
 a_t = \rho_{\max}\,\operatorname{sigmoid}(g_a(H_t)),
+
 $$
 
+
+
 $$
+
 \widehat y_t = a_t \odot \widehat y_{t-1}
+
              + (1-a_t)\odot u_t.
+
 $$
 
+
+
 Here H[t] depends only on observable inputs up to t. The feedback is the model's own previous output, never a true target. The recurrence operates on two scalars, one per target.
 
+
+
 Proposed initialization:
 
+
+
 - rho_max = 0.99, with a separate 0.95 cap arm only if needed.
+
 - Initialize gate-head weights to zero.
+
 - Initialize gate-head bias to logit(0.10 / 0.99), so every initial gate is 0.10.
+
 - Reset the two-value AR state to zero at the start of each sequence.
+
 - Update it on every row, including all 99 warmup rows and unscored rows.
+
 - Do not clip the AR state to the official scoring range during training by default.
+
 - The exact non-AR control fixes a[t] = 0, yielding yhat[t] = u[t].
 
+
+
 This is a learned input-dependent persistence term. It can preserve a previous estimate in quiet periods and refresh it on informative inputs. It can also oversmooth fast changes, create lag, or learn a redundant state; those are explicit failure hypotheses. Fixed output smoothing and this jointly trained gate are different recipes, and neither is presumed beneficial.
 
+
+
 The gate's instantaneous derivative with respect to the previous output, holding the current observable-derived backbone output fixed, is a[t]. Thus each one-step feedback coefficient is bounded below 1. This does not establish a generalization improvement, good calibration, or a universal numerical-stability guarantee for the entire learned network.
 
+
+
 Keep the feedback OUTSIDE the Transformer input. If yesterday's predicted output is injected into today's Transformer token, a complete teacher rollout requires sequential backbone calls, and the intended time-parallel training path is lost.
 
+
+
 For the proposed readout, let b[t] = (1-a[t])u[t]. Affine recurrence pairs compose associatively:
 
+
+
 $$
+
 (a_2,b_2)\circ(a_1,b_1)=(a_2a_1,\ b_2+a_2b_1).
+
 $$
 
+
+
 Consequently, training can compute all H[t], u[t], and a[t] in parallel and evaluate the small recurrence with a differentiable prefix scan. This algebra is our derivation. Gated linear-attention literature [S9] supplies a related hardware-aware recurrence precedent, not evidence for this particular readout.
 
+
+
 A production scan must have a verified backward implementation. Do not assume an experimental scan API supports autograd or all requested dtypes. Avoid formulations that divide by a long cumulative product: products can underflow over 20,000 rows. A sequential FP32 recurrence is the correctness reference; a blocked associative scan is the optimization candidate. A CPU/Python loop over all rows is not an acceptable throughput assumption.
 
+
+
 ### 4. A separate auxiliary autoregressive learning term
 
+
+
 Add an optional head predicting future changes in observable features:
 
+
+
 $$
+
 \Delta x_{t,h}=x_{t+h}-x_t,\quad h\in\{1,8\},
+
 $$
 
+
+
 $$
+
 \mathcal L_{\mathrm{aux}}
+
 =\operatorname{mean}_{t,h,j}\,
+
 \operatorname{Huber}\left(
+
 \frac{\widehat{\Delta x}_{t,h,j}-\Delta x_{t,h,j}}{s_j}
+
 \right).
+
 $$
 
+
+
 The scale s[j] is fitted on fitting groups only, floored away from zero, and frozen for evaluation. Exclude cross-sequence pairs and out-of-range horizons. Predict the designated observable feature columns, excluding sequence identity, scoring flags, and target columns.
 
+
+
 Future observations are auxiliary TARGETS during fitting, never inputs available to the representation at t. This distinction must survive tokenization, normalization, augmentation, caching, and batching.
 
+
+
 Start with beta_aux = 0.05 only after defining both supervised and auxiliary terms as normalized means. Log their separate losses and shared-backbone gradient norms: a numerical coefficient alone does not fix their relative gradient contribution. Zero changes may dominate this task; report change/no-change diagnostics. Reweighting changed rows or adding an update-indicator objective is another arm, not an invisible repair.
 
+
+
 The next-observation auxiliary task and learned output recurrence answer different questions. Neither requires a language-model softmax or discrete vocabulary.
 
+
+
 ### 5. Train four teacher variants as a factorial comparison
 
+
+
 | Arm | Learned output AR | Observable-change auxiliary loss |
+
 |---|---:|---:|
+
 | T0 | No | No |
+
 | T1 | Yes | No |
+
 | T2 | No | Yes |
+
 | T3 | Yes | Yes |
 
+
+
 Keep the backbone, fitting groups, target treatment, optimizer, update horizon, and checkpoint-selection rule matched. Record tiny parameter-count differences.
 
+
+
 Primary contrasts are T1−T0, T2−T0, and interaction T3−T1−T2+T0. The interaction is measured on the declared score endpoint; no gain is assumed additive. Evaluate both raw u[t] and final yhat[t] diagnostically, but freeze the selected served/teacher output before comparison outcomes.
 
+
+
 ### 6. Supervised objective and target semantics
 
+
+
 A concrete proposed baseline uses:
 
+
+
 $$
+
 c(y)=\operatorname{clip}(y,-2,2),\qquad
+
 w(y)=0.05+|c(y)|,
+
 $$
 
+
+
 $$
+
 \mathcal L_{\mathrm{sup}}
+
 =\frac12\sum_{k=0}^1
+
 \frac{\sum_t m_t w(y_{t,k})
+
 (\widehat y_{t,k}-c(y_{t,k}))^2}
+
 {\sum_t m_t w(y_{t,k})}.
+
 $$
 
+
+
 The training mask m excludes warmup, padding, repeated prefix rows, and rows outside declared fitting membership. It does not pretend the hidden test scoring mask is observed. The available fitting-source scoring-mask/propensity policy must be declared; the primary simple recipe above uses all otherwise eligible fitting rows and no newly learned propensity model.
 
+

 ### 7. Chunking, state, and context are part of the architecture
 
+
+
 Proposed starting layout: 1024 new core rows plus up to 3072 preceding raw rows, giving an input length up to 4096. Enumerate nonoverlapping cores in sequence order so every eligible fitting row is a supervised core row once per epoch. Pad partial final cores and mask padding.
 
+
+
 Within each window, attention is causal. Core rows have approximately 3072–4095 preceding rows available once away from the sequence start, rather than an identical 4096-row rolling history for every output. This is an anchored overlapping-window model. Do not label it an exact full-sequence or exact rolling-window Transformer.
 
+
+
 Recompute prefix representations under current weights. Only core outputs advance the persistent AR state; replayed prefix rows must not update that state twice. At the first window of a sequence, include the initial rows and perform warmup state updates. Carry the two-value output state across cores; detach it at the declared training TBPTT boundary. This truncates the recurrence gradient across cores and must be recorded.
 
+
+
 Contiguous sequence slots stay on their assigned rank until completion. An optimizer update between cores means the carried training state was formed under slightly older weights; that is a declared truncated-training approximation. Evaluation/export uses fixed weights for the complete sequence and has no such optimizer-state drift.
 
+
+
 Teacher-target export must use the same anchored window definition and row positions. Changing window anchors, replacing it with a different rolling KV cache, or resetting state at each chunk changes the model and must be measured. Merely carrying a KV cache across all layers is not automatically equivalent to recomputing the raw prefix.
 
+
+
 Long-context arms change the prefix/window lengths explicitly. Transformer-XL-style detached hidden memory [S2] is a separate architecture/training arm. A per-layer sliding attention width can yield a larger stacked receptive field; do not confuse it with a hard bound on total input history.

 ## Distillation into GRU

 ### 8. Why this can be distilled, and what is not guaranteed
 
+
+
 After freezing teacher weights and using its own recurrent outputs, the teacher is a deterministic causal function of x[0:t]. Its AR state contains no privileged target information. A GRU can be trained on that function without receiving the Transformer, its attention states, or its previous teacher output at inference.
 
+
+
 This establishes information compatibility, not representational equivalence. Finite student capacity, different memory, optimization, or a teacher's brittle fine-scale behavior can prevent successful transfer. Teacher-score improvement is therefore insufficient for selecting the teacher. The final endpoint is the trained student's official score and its contribution to the frozen submission blend. Distillation-capacity literature motivates this separation [S6]; it does not guarantee transfer here.
 
+
+
 Export continuous two-value teacher predictions with dropout disabled, complete sequence state/reset, and pinned precision/window semantics. Use FP32 output storage as the reference; two outputs for all 249.6M supplied rows occupy about 1.997 decimal GB before IDs/provenance. This is arithmetic, not a measured cache format.

 ### 9. Two student architectures
 
+
+

 S1 uses the same GRU backbone plus the same two-value learned AR readout. It adds explicit output recurrence to the student's state. At deployment, the GRU needs only its hidden state and two previous predictions; u[t] and a[t] come from its own representation. Gate initialization, sequence reset, and warmup updates follow the teacher's contract. Its actual package/runtime/ABI are later submission-engineering measurements.

+
 For both students, primary targets are the teacher's final FREE-RUNNING yhat[t]. Do not train the student using the teacher's previous prediction as a feedback input and then replace it with its own previous prediction at deployment. That distribution mismatch is unnecessary. True previous targets are unavailable as inputs in both teacher and student.

 Scheduled sampling [S4] discusses a related train/inference feedback mismatch in sequence generation, but does not make lagged hidden future-price labels valid features in this competition. The primary plan uses free-running predictions throughout and does not introduce scheduled sampling.

 ### 15. DDP recipe and exact loss normalization
 
+
+
 Use one process per GPU, a complete model replica per rank, and NCCL for GPU gradient communication [S10, S16]. Start with ordinary DDP; these model sizes do not by themselves justify model sharding, tensor parallelism, or FSDP. Activation memory and throughput still require real profiles.
 
+
+
 At 86M parameters, FP32 weights, gradients, and two Adam moment arrays alone account for approximately 16 bytes/parameter, or 1.38 decimal GB per replica. This excludes activations, attention workspace, communication buffers, temporary optimizer arrays and allocator overhead; it is not a complete admission bound. The attention/window implementation can dominate the memory footprint.
 
+
+
 Candidate launch shape, illustrative only:
 
+
+
     torchrun --standalone --nnodes=1 --nproc-per-node=8 \
+
       train_transformer_teacher.py --config <frozen-recipe.json>
 
+
+
 No such new trainer or runnable command is implemented by this note. A multi-node deployment needs a real rendezvous/network configuration; the single-node command is not a claim about the user's topology.
 
+
+
 Candidate global batch target: 65,536 NEW core rows/update. For 1024-row cores, world size 8, microbatch 8 sequence slots/rank, accumulation 1 gives 8 × 8 × 1024. Equivalent example: microbatch 2/rank with accumulation 4. These are target shapes to profile, not safe capacity certificates.
 
+
+
 Use no_sync on the first accumulation microsteps, enclosing BOTH forward and backward [S10, S11]. Synchronize on the last microstep, clip once, step once, and advance the scheduler once per successful optimizer update.
 
+
+
 For weighted supervision, let A[r,j,k] be the weighted squared-error SUM on rank r, microstep j, target k. Let W[k] be the globally summed effective weight across all ranks and microsteps in the current optimizer update. Because DDP averages rank gradients, use:
 
+
+
 $$
+
 L_{r,j}=\frac{R}{2}\sum_{k=0}^{1}\frac{A_{r,j,k}}{W_k},
+
 $$
 
+
+
 where R is world size. Accumulating these local backward contributions and then allowing DDP averaging produces the gradient of the globally normalized per-target loss, provided weights/masks are fixed data-derived quantities. Do not additionally divide by accumulation count: W already spans the whole update. Auxiliary/KD terms need their own correctly defined denominators.
 
+
+
 This is our derived implementation contract. Uniform equal-count, unweighted batches can use simpler average-loss rules, but unequal scoring weights, padding, and partial chunks make naive means-of-local-means incorrect. All ranks must participate in collectives in the same order. If W[k] is zero, handle that target coherently on all ranks.
 
+
+
 Precompute the per-update global denominators from the planned microbatch labels/masks before backward, or use a mathematically equivalent gradient-rescaling implementation. Do not retain every forward graph merely to discover denominators later. This formula assumes default DDP gradient averaging; a custom communication hook that changes reduction semantics needs its own derivation.
 
+
+
 DDP/data requirements:
 
+
+
 - Deterministically shard sequence slots and keep each active sequence on one rank.
+
 - Shuffle sequences per epoch; never shuffle rows within a live sequence.
+
 - Set the distributed sampler epoch where that sampler is used; preserve its actual seed/state [S14].
+
 - Avoid sampler-padding duplication of effective training/evaluation examples. Explicit zero-weight padding can equalize the final distributed step.
+
 - Keep dummy ranks graph-connected and participating in collective operations.
+
 - Prefix/warmup/padding rows update only their valid state semantics and never inflate the supervised denominator.
+
 - Do not split one recurrent sequence across ranks without an implemented, audited state handoff.
+
 - Start with find_unused_parameters false only if every trainable branch really participates; the auxiliary-disabled model must not leave unhandled unused heads.
+
 - Enable static_graph only after the implementation satisfies its contract, not because the config name sounds static.
+
 - Pin rank-specific RNG, data order, accumulation position, per-slot sequence IDs, next row offsets, and carried states in resumable checkpoints.
+
 - Record nondeterministic training kernels. Deployment determinism and repeatable reset remain separate requirements.
 
+
+
 For validation, reduce the official sufficient statistics over all ranks and compute the final correlation once. Averaging rank-local correlations is not the official global metric. Avoid duplicated evaluation rows from a generic padded DistributedSampler.

 1. **Teacher frontier:** full outer-fold WP, per-target/slice scores, compute and context. This describes the teacher, not student transfer.
+
 2. **Transfer frontier:** the *same* student, optimizer, labels, masks and budget trained from each teacher. Rank its actual WP delta and fitting cost. Also report weighted teacher-imitation error and residual correlation with the strong GRU; low imitation error alone is not success.
+
 3. **Release frontier:** frozen student or complete blend after CPU export. Rank actual callback quality, total runtime, resident memory and ZIP bytes. A fast incomplete export does not enter this frontier.
 
+
+
 Use an immutable teacher registry, one record per fold/seed/checkpoint: source and architecture hashes; checkpoint SHA256; source-qualified fitting and inner-selection component hashes; full ancestor graph including propensity/normalization/initializer; precision; selected epoch/rule; context/position/AR semantics; raw-output and optional hint-cache manifests; eligible purpose (`outer_clean`, `fit_in_sample_targets`, `production_only`, `unknown`). Missing membership is `unknown`, never an empty fitting set. Alias/duplicate components across both supplied sources belong to the same exclusion unit.
 
+
+
 For each outer fold, choose checkpoints by a predetermined terminal epoch or an inner fitting-only rule. Never use the outer fold to select a teacher and then quote that same fold as unbiased transfer confirmation. The initial packets avoid this selection loop: they fix the 207M L teacher in advance for hints and streaming, and compare L/XL explicitly in the capacity packet. Selecting a later production winner from exposed development results is allowed operationally, but must retain selection history and unknown public transfer.
 
+
+
 The new `teacher-transfer-frontier` packet tests four target sources (labels only, clean strong GRU, L207M, XL682M) crossed with two cold GRU students (H256×2, H512×2): **eight arms, 240 student fits**, plus up to90 teacher fits for three30-cell teacher families if no eligible exact caches exist. Each cell's teacher is shared across the two student capacities; it is not two independent teachers. The primary contrasts are XL−L for each capacity, their difference-in-differences, and all four L/XL student-versus-matched-label-only contrasts. A better teacher contrast does not justify KD if both students lose to their label-only controls. An XL teacher that improves only H512 changes the student/assistant allocation; an XL teacher that improves neither despite higher teacher WP argues against buying more teacher scale for this student recipe. It does not close large teachers generally. GRU and label-only arms keep practical baselines visible without attributing historical recipe differences to architecture.

 ### 23. Freeze cache semantics before spending on teacher scale
 
+
+
 Export teacher outputs with fixed weights, dropout disabled and the exact free-running forward definition. The cache key includes data SHA, source name, row-group/component identity, sequence and row position, teacher checkpoint, normalizer, window anchoring, positional rule, warmup/reset, output head and precision. Integer group IDs alone are insufficient across train/valid. Bind the exact served t0/t1 head mapping, any inverse target transform and units; the current strong GRU teacher has auxiliary outputs, so taking the first two columns without a verified export mapping is forbidden. Write atomic complete shards with row counts, shape, dtype, SHA256 and completion markers; partial exports cannot be training inputs.
 
+
+
 Preserve all causal rows for state updates. The student loss mask excludes padding/warmup and disallowed fitting rows; it never drops intermediate rows from the recurrent input stream. No teacher output, uncertainty, latent hint or teacher-forced label becomes a student inference input. Teacher hidden hints must be the hidden state at that row, computed without future observations. Future auxiliary labels may supervise a causal model, but cannot be cached as its input representation.
 
+
+
 The default is **in-sample teacher targets on outer-fitting components**, clearly labeled. This is not outer leakage when all teacher ancestors exclude the outer fold, but it can transfer memorization. A nested crossfit-cache comparison is a continuation of PR #3/#12: partition outer-fitting components into K=3 source-qualified groups; train3 inner teachers, each excluding its target shard and the entire outer evaluation; stitch predictions by exact row key. Compare against ordinary in-sample targets using identical student fits. Extra teacher fits and smaller teacher training sets are part of this treatment, so any gain is not attributed solely to leakage removal. A three-teacher in-sample ensemble at matched total teacher-fit count is the useful cost/diversity control. Freeze inner partitions before labels/results. Do not silently substitute a crossfit cache into the new packets.
 
+
+
 Cache arithmetic is a capacity planning input: two FP32 predictions cost `8N` bytes; a64-dimensional FP32 hint costs `256N`. At249.6million rows these are about2.0GB and63.9GB before identifiers/manifests. Export only admissible fitting membership for each cell, on physical storage. Compression/quantization of hints is a separate treatment; scientific caches remain FP32. A streaming sharded reader avoids multiplying RAM by the total cache size, but disk throughput must be measured with the actual teacher/student pipeline.

 ### 24. Output KD versus intermediate knowledge
 
+
+
 Two scalar predictions may discard teacher features useful to the GRU. Conversely, forcing a GRU to copy attention coordinates may consume capacity and worsen the task. `teacher-representation-hints` makes this falsifiable with a fixed L207M teacher and the same H256×2 student:

 | Arm | Common output objective | Additional fitting-only supervision |

 All arms contain the same student projection `P: H256→64`; discard it at export because it neither feeds recurrent state nor the final head. Teacher target is the final pre-readout hidden vector projected by a fixed seed14019 random matrix `R[d,64] ~ N(0,1/d)`, followed by coordinate centering/scaling fitted only on fitting hints (scale floor1e-6). Record R and moment hashes. The proposed hint term is the mean of `(P(hS_t)-zT_t)^2` over eligible rows and64 coordinates, coefficient0.1. No teacher/student coordinate equality is assumed and no fitted reduction uses outer rows. Output KD remains correctly aligned in all arms. Report the number of excluded hint rows.

 Primary contrasts H−O and H−P distinguish useful aligned knowledge from extra training loss/regularization. Report hint and task gradient norms separately; matching coefficient does not match gradient scale. H−P can still reflect the negative control being harmful, so H−O is indispensable.  ## Limits and validity
 
+
+
 The AR term may learn nothing beyond the Transformer/GRU hidden state. It may improve fit but hurt the clipped global metric, lag fast events, or transfer poorly to a constrained student. A teacher can improve while its student degrades. A mixed teacher can help despite a weaker individual member; measure that complete path.
 
+
+
 Different input encoders, raw/clipped targets, propensity weighting, warm parents, context semantics, and precision are material recipe changes. Unmatched comparisons cannot isolate the autoregressive mechanism.
 
+
+
 Full-sequence replay with fixed weights is required for teacher targets and student evaluation. Associative scan algebra does not establish numerical equivalence at every dtype or a working autograd kernel. Future-observation auxiliary labels are legal fitting targets only when they cannot enter the forward input or preprocessing state at the predicted row.
 
+
+
 Compute availability is user-reported. No cluster admission, paid spending, software installation, or job launch is performed by this document. Local CPU/scratch limits continue to apply to support work.

+
+
 Before any future scientific fit, the implementation must establish causal future-perturbation invariance, full-20k sequential-versus-scan output and gradient agreement, correct initial/warmup/sequence reset, no double update of AR state on replayed prefixes, teacher export/reload repeatability, and single-process-versus-DDP weighted-update agreement with unequal masks and padding. Test numerical equivalence with dropout disabled and a fixed reference dtype. These are specified future engineering checks, not checks performed for this documentation task.
 
+
+
 Prepare matched T0/T1 teacher pairs at the reference and primary L/XL scales, with T2/T3 as explicit auxiliary/interaction siblings. AdamW is the reference optimizer; quality-first 12/24/48-epoch WSD routes, larger/full-context teachers, Muon comparisons and heterogeneous ensembles remain active proposals under Section 19. The six-epoch warmup/cosine model is a control rather than the final capacity/horizon preference. Keep strict FP32 as the reference until numerical policy is explicitly resolved; no quantization is proposed.
 
+
+
 Before a future fit: freeze component manifests, architecture/loss/precision configs, scan/window/export semantics, exact optimizer groups, checkpoint policy, seed/fold matrix, GPU-hour budget, and the actual cluster profile. Then own each fit through checkpoints, complete causal predictions, official evaluation, and matched student training.

 The scientific deliverable is the comparison of trained students, including failed transfer. A trained teacher alone is an intermediate artifact.

+# Groupwise fast/slow Kalman innovation states
+
+**Status: the exposed train-row ridge proxy and a matched two-seed recurrent interaction screen are complete. The additive ridge arm is negative; the recurrent paired effect is tiny and changes sign across seeds on exposed F0. Keep the feature family open without promoting a stable gain.**
+
+## Mechanism
+
+The all-channel Kalman screen found that innovation magnitude varies by feature family and sequence position, while its scalar CUSUM becomes saturated early. This motivates a narrower representation test: retain every raw input, then add three causal statistics for each of the 13 predeclared state groups—fast innovation energy, slow innovation energy and the fast-to-slow log ratio.
+
+The intended mechanism is conditional state information. A fast increase can mark a local change; the slow level can describe the sequence's current background noise; their ratio can indicate a transient departure from that background. The features are computed from input-only, pre-update standardized innovations. All Kalman and EMA state resets at each sequence boundary. No future rows, targets, scoring masks or target feedback enter the extractor.
+
+## Test
+
+The [experiment packet](../../campaign_2026-10-18/online_features_r1/group_fast_slow_r1/README.md) predeclares three matched representations: raw 112 inputs, raw plus the existing scalar clock, and raw plus 39 groupwise fast/slow state features. A two-output weighted ridge screen uses same-row `x[t] → y[t]` alignment after the 99-row warmup; features use every post-warmup row and the fit uses a fixed stride of 10. Components, not rows, define four cross-fit folds. The label-blind predictions are frozen before any held-out labels are opened. Because `train.parquet` has no `is_scored` column, the initial official-mask grader correctly stopped. The separate [train-row proxy grade recipe](../../campaign_2026-10-18/online_features_r1/group_fast_slow_r1/grade_train_proxy_r1.json) uses every target-bearing row from step 99 onward and applies the official metric formula with a different, explicitly nonofficial selection mask.
+
+The source sample contains 32 components previously selected from `fold0.fit.train` for the innovation distribution screen. They are already exposed development data. A one-sequence exact-path profile used 1.122 GB worker memory under a 2 GB cap; the full 32-component label-blind fit/prediction used 1.253 GB under the same cap. Both had zero OOM/max deltas; these are resource receipts, not quality evidence. Component cross-fitting is useful for an allocation decision but does not create a clean validation result or capture seed variation. Any proxy score uses all post-warmup train rows, not an official validation mask, and position bins and paired component resampling remain conditional on these four fixed fits.
+
+## Decision rule
+
+A stable, practical increment over raw that appears across folds can justify a matched recurrent screen. A small or uncertain linear delta does not close Kalman feature research; it only defers this exact fast/slow encoding. A separate B300 draft requires a larger direction: a recurrent interaction with the state features that is materially distinct from existing causal-innovation and learned-Kalman handoffs. No such handoff follows from the earlier distribution screen alone.
+
+## Result and interpretation
+
+The frozen label-blind cross-fit was graded separately as an all-post-warmup train-row proxy because the source has no official `is_scored` mask. Raw scored 0.26885894 WP; raw plus the scalar clock scored 0.26875090 (Δ −0.00010803, paired component-bootstrap 95% interval [−0.00243463, +0.00189382]); raw plus the 39 group states scored 0.25576581 (Δ −0.01309313, interval [−0.03369300, +0.00595564]). The group-state arm lost in every one of the four cross-fit folds and each of the four position bins; its largest bin loss was −0.062789 WP at steps 500–1,999. The scalar clock is effectively tied on this proxy.
+
+This is evidence against using these 39 summaries as a simple additive feature block in the frozen weighted-ridge treatment. It does not establish that the group states lack nonlinear or recurrent conditional value. The 32 components were selected for earlier feature diagnostics and are exposed; the bootstrap conditions on four fixed fitted models and does not include fit-seed or selection uncertainty. The score uses every train target row from step 99 onward under the official metric formula, but this is not the official validation mask or score. Data identity pins the source footer/metadata, not the complete Parquet payload. See the experiment packet and the independent [result review](../reviews/GROUPWISE_FAST_SLOW_PROXY_RESULT_REVIEW_20261018_R1.md).
+
+**Allocation:** defer this exact additive ridge arm. Keep the broader causal Kalman direction open. +# From useful i1 inputs to a function-preserving history test
+
+## Question or claim
+
+Can explicit causal history contribute information that the GRU does not retain,
+even when the history model scores worse alone? Preserve the sequence of
+observations and changing explanations, rather than recording only a winner.
+This snapshot was requested by the user after the intermediate-results discussion.
+
+## Mechanism and method
+
+The frozen screen uses cold H512×1, the same 367 input slots, 10% of fitting
+components as complete sequences, three epochs and fixed checkpoint 2. Cells
+are F0/seed1001 and F2/seed1002. A masks standard and derived i1 channels;
+B uses standard inputs with history slots masked; C activates residuals from
+causal EMA half-lives 32/512 and slow change energy. There are six new fits,
+two per arm, no teacher fits and no reused fitted controls. Metric and fixed
+90%B/10%C mixture are unchanged; coefficients were not searched.
+
+## Evidence and interpretation
+
+1. **The original information question:** perhaps i1 contributes little at this
+   fidelity. Removing it instead costs 0.01590144 on F0 and 0.01110844 on F2.
+   Standard i1 is useful in both cells; this does not show which history
+   representation will help or establish a broad capacity conclusion.
+2. **The first apparent contradiction:** F0 C−B is −0.00353711, yet the fixed
+   90%B/10%C mixture gains +0.00035953. Its conditional paired-component 95%
+   interval is [−0.00001187,+0.00070893]; target deltas are +0.00052218 and
+   +0.00019688. A weaker model can supply a useful correction. All four overall
+   position-bin point deltas improve, but early t1 bins lose. This is one
+   exposed cell, not an established ensemble improvement.
+3. **A distribution explanation was checked:** the same F0 mixture gains
+   +0.00036506 before prediction clipping and +0.00035953 under official
+   clipping. Clipping slightly reduces the gain. The correction has positive
+   target covariance after accounting for B for both targets. This weakens
+   clipping-only and pure scalar-shrinkage explanations; it does not prove
+   that temporal information caused the correction. This decomposition reuses
+   the same fits and supplies no independent replication or extra uncertainty
+   interval.
+4. **A source-level confound changes the next test:** identical stored initial
+   weights do not mean identical initial functions. C activates 156 appended
+   random input columns that B masks after normalization. History exposure
+   and the resulting optimization path therefore change together. The cold
+   result may reflect useful information, a different training trajectory, or
+   both; no conditioning effect has been measured.
+5. **Latest standalone observation:** F2 C has now scored 0.6802047933 versus
+   B 0.6841082148, C−B −0.0039034215 (t0 −0.0029051558;
+   t1 −0.0049016872). Both history models are weaker alone. At this snapshot,
+   the complete-panel grader is still running: the F2 fixed mixture and
+   paired intervals are pending. Do not transfer the F0 mixture conclusion
+   to F2 or select a mechanism from F0 alone.
+
+## Limits and validity
+
+All evaluation folds are exposed. Component intervals condition on the fitted
+models and do not quantify seed variation, fold variation or public transfer;
+two fold/seed cells cannot separate these axes. The screen is a small cold
+training comparison, not evidence of a production improvement. Strong parents
+have different initializer/cache ancestry and need within-cell matched controls.
+
+Separate endpoint checks also matter: replaying TL3 on the current native host
+leaves the H512 replacement gap near −0.00736292. A fixed FP32 counterfactual
+on eight exposed components gains only +0.00004035 over native CP5 and leaves
+−0.00328280 versus TL3 on that sample. Runtime/precision differences therefore
+do not explain those measured gaps; unknown TL3 ancestry and member utility
+remain alternatives. Do not infer a public score or architecture verdict.
+
+## Decision and next step
+
+The new falsifier is **function-preserving history introduction**: extend a
+strong 211-input parent to 367 slots with zero appended projection weights,
+retain its original normalization bitwise, and give both arms identical,
+explicit fitting-only statistics for the appended slots. Verify parent-output
+parity before fitting. Then compare masked/unmasked history with identical
+sampling, objective and two-epoch continuation. This distinguishes incremental
+history learning from an immediate random change to the inherited predictor.
+
+Conditional implementation is prepared on commit
+`cc9af1c68745289a71e30aa45e5242af87a3f5bf`: default-off normalization option,
+restricted inheritance guards and synthetic tests. Static checks pass; tests
+and independent source review are still pending. No warm fit is admitted by
+this note. Selection waits for the complete two-cell panel and fixed endpoint
+contribution; any follow-up uses the existing four-fit F0/F1 allocation, zero
+new teachers, sustained resource profiling and no history/auxiliary combination.
+
+Serving is a separate gate: active history is not wired into the native raw-row
+callback, and the current native layout rejects 367 inputs. A useful screen
+must still earn strong-control improvement and actual complete endpoint
+quality/runtime before production. Better auxiliary prediction alone likewise
+does not earn a larger dynamics run.

+# Innovation-conditioned latent gain inside a GRU
+
+## Question
+
+Can a causal, task-trained latent prediction-correction operator make a GRU teacher represent state changes more usefully, and can a standard GRU student retain that information through the existing teacher-cache route?
+
+## Mechanism
+
+For encoded input `z_t`, the observer forms a latent measurement `o_t`, predicts a local-linear prior `m^-_t` from the previous two encoded rows, computes innovation `nu_t = o_t - m^-_t`, and estimates a bounded diagonal gain:
+
+```text
+m^-_t = o_(t-1) + sigmoid(a) * (o_(t-1) - o_(t-2))
+nu_t  = o_t - m^-_t
+K_t   = sigmoid(b + gain_net([o_t, nu_t]))
+m_t   = m^-_t + K_t * nu_t
+```
+
+The posterior and gain-weighted innovation enter zero-initialized residual branches connected to the ordinary fused GRU input and readout. State carries across trainer chunks and resets at sequence boundaries. The model weights remain fixed at inference; this is causal state adaptation, not test-time weight learning or an online-label update.
+
+## Why it might help
+
+The neighboring fixed output filters hurt, the additive 39-state groupwise ridge encoding lost on a nonofficial train-row proxy, and a two-seed recurrent append screen changed sign around zero. A small fixed local-trend input replay was positive but uncertain. These results weaken fixed transforms and naive feature appends while leaving open whether a learned gain used conditionally inside a recurrent update contributes something the GRU gates do not learn naturally. They are not evidence that this observer will help.
+
+The final competition value must be a better served standard-GRU student under the same fold, cache, target scale, coefficient, seed and training budget. A teacher-only gain is insufficient if its representation does not transfer.
+
+## Frozen comparison proposed before the stop
+
+At H512×2, compare scratch-trained ordinary GRU, context-only observer, and innovation-conditioned observer on paired source-qualified fold/seed cells. The context-only arm masks innovation only at the gain-network input; both observer arms still apply gain-times-innovation correction. It is therefore a narrow conditioning ablation, not a no-innovation observer. The standard-GRU student comparison would use matched existing, context-teacher-replacement and innovation-teacher-replacement caches.
+
+The proposal specified 30 paired cells, four previously exposed folds, and fold/seed/component reporting. These folds are not fresh holdouts. The detailed run matrix, FP32 recipe and logging plan live in the local draft identified below.
+
+## Current status and blockers
+
+Implementation exists only in the isolated local worktree `/home/vlad/development/wunder/research_tmp/kalman_innovation_gain_gru_b300`, branch `experiment/kalman-innovation-gain-gru-b300`, commit `527d2e985`. It was not pushed; no pull request exists. No fit, student cache, B300 profile, synthetic invariant check, score, or submission exists. The local read-only implementation review found no causal/chunk-state defect by inspection but identified three material prefit blockers:
+
+1. Synthetic prefix-invariance, chunk/full-sequence, reset and batch-isolation checks have not run.
+2. The actual H512 B300 profile has not run; eight B300 cards are an intended resource target, not measured availability.
+3. The per-cell clean teacher-source registry is null, so the student-cache experiment cannot be launched faithfully.
+
+The user stopped new research admission on 2026-10-18. Preserve this as an untested local code draft. Do not treat the stale branch-side PR #22 text as publication evidence; no PR #22 was created. The larger published handoffs already on record are [#14](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/14), [#17](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/17), and [#18](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/18).

+# Causal Kalman filtering of model outputs
+
+## Question or claim
+
+Can causal filtering of the model's own prediction stream improve the endpoint while preserving the model's raw-input training distribution?
+
+## Mechanism and method
+
+The frozen CPU screen compares the unchanged parent predictions with a fixed steady-state local-level Kalman filter (`Q/R=0.25`) and a per-sequence/channel `Q/R` estimate from the first 99 model outputs. The initial 99 rows are unscored calibration/warmup; scored rows use only the prefix and current/past predictions. Both filters reset at sequence boundaries and read no labels or masks during prediction. Details and exact pins are in the [campaign packet](../../campaign_2026-10-18/online_features_r1/kalman_output_filter_r1/README.md).
+
+## Evidence and interpretation
+
+This frozen screen has completed. On 468 previously inspected F0 groups/141 components, raw parent scored 0.6812265 WP, the fixed filter 0.6755207, and the prefix-estimated filter 0.6647620. Differences from raw were −0.0057059 (95% component-bootstrap CI [−0.0065918, −0.0050088]) and −0.0164645 (CI [−0.0190768, −0.0144069]). Both lost in all four descriptive component partitions.
+
+## Limits and validity
+
+The comparison uses the repeatedly inspected F0 panel and a single fixed parent checkpoint. Component-bootstrap intervals condition on that endpoint and cannot establish clean CV, training-seed variation or public transfer. The filter can introduce lag; the adaptive noise estimate is a heuristic from model outputs, not observed target feedback. This result does not test learned Kalman input/hidden-state features, teacher quality, student transfer or true online learning.
+
+## Decision and next step
+
+The predeclared follow-up threshold was not met, so do not continue tuning these two output-filter recipes on exposed F0 or submit them. This does not close the larger retained-raw Kalman feature teacher/student direction in [draft PR #17](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/17), nor broader online adaptation. No new B300 draft is warranted by this inference-only negative result.

+
+
 ## Decision and scope
 
+

 Build a strong numerical causal Transformer, then measure the quality that can

 The local October20 plan remains governed by its existing budget and start.

 Strict FP32, no autocast and no TF32 remain binding. Keeping FP32 model weights
+
 while computing attention or Muon orthogonalization in BF16 would violate this

 contract. A future precision change would be an explicit new experiment.

+
+## Latest user source: TradeFM and observable transition likelihood
+
+The user supplied [TradeFM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23784) after the initial
+scale design. Its event-modeling mechanism motivates our proposed
+[observable-event adaptation](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/research/experiment_drafts/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/TRADEFM_ADAPTATION.md):
+retain raw rows and supervised targets, add next-change survival and mark losses,
+and test them at fixed0.68B capacity before spending on the whole scale ladder.
+This comparison costs four new fits; the0.68B/1.65B capacity screen is a separate
+four-fit allocation. The source's distributional generation results do not
+establish weighted-Pearson or GRU transfer. Anonymous columns do not justify
+copying price/volume/timestamp formulas. The addendum preserves the actual
+source inspection, our censoring/causality adaptation and independent scout review.
+
 ## What the B300 results tell us
 
+
+
 The [partial B300 review](../reviews/B300_PR_RUN_UPDATE_REVIEW_20261019_R1.md)
+
 compares GRUs, not Transformers. Width beat depth slightly in the R01 recipe;
+
 the tested geometry bundle was negative; age/innovation had no paired scores.
+
 None establishes a Transformer ceiling or an effective Transformer feature set.
+
 In particular, do not insert the entire geometry bank into the default teacher.
+
 Retain it as a distinct representation branch if a mechanism warrants revisiting.
 
+
+
 Anchor quality to the strongest available source-qualified recurrent teacher,
+
 not only to a weak labels-only GRU. Reuse its exact clean fold predictions where
+
 available. TL3 is a useful complete-endpoint comparator, but its unknown fitting
+
 ancestry must remain explicit; a replay is not automatically clean CV. A win
+
 between two new Transformers does not establish that either improves that anchor.
 
+
+
 ## Architecture and numeric embeddings
 
+
+
 Use one complete observation row per temporal token. Preserve all 112 raw values
+
 and the canonical 99 event features as the reference input, with fitting-only
+
 feature scales. Compare against the identical raw-only encoder if event features
+
 prove redundant. Never turn 112 feature columns into 112 extra time positions.
+
 Sequence IDs and scoring flags are not model inputs.
 
+
+
 The representation ladder is deliberately separable:
 
+
+
 1. **Dense reference:** an MLP from the ordered 211 values to the model width.
+
 2. **Grouped numerical encoder:** use the supplied 13 groups (six per instrument
+
    plus additional features), attaching each event channel through a reviewed
+
    semantic registry. Per-group small MLPs produce 128-dimensional representations;
+
    concatenate and project into the temporal width, retaining a direct raw-row
+
    residual projection. Do not add this on top of a changed attention/loss and
+
    then attribute the whole effect to grouping.
+
 3. **Richer scalar basis:** fitting-only piecewise-linear numeric embeddings,
+
    initially 8–16 bins per selected channel, retain the raw scalar and an explicit
+
    missing/nonfinite indicator where required by the data contract. Periodic
+
    scalar embeddings are an alternative basis, not evidence of a periodic process.
+
 4. **Local dynamics branch:** causal lag differences at 1/4/16/64 rows, log1p age
+
    since observable updates, or a small left-padded dilated convolution. Keep raw
+
    values. Compare one branch at a time; full-sequence statistics and centered
+
    smoothing are invalid for early outputs. Rolling features are optional tools,
+
    not a requirement that large models must consume a large manual feature bank.
 
+
+
 A learned causal GRU/filter stem pretrained on observable changes is another
+

+

+

+

 ## Context, attention and causal long memory
 
+
+
 The first scalable reference is dense causal attention over 4096 rows, with a
+
 2048-row left prefix and a 2048-row scored core. Prefix rows provide context but
+
 are not duplicated in the fitting loss. Early cores use all available prefix
+
 with padding masked. At export, reproduce these exact window/position semantics;
+
 do not compare a short-window teacher cache with an unrelated full-history model.
+
 This reference has bounded context, not the whole 20k sequence.
 
+
+
 For the full-history challenger, preserve a fast row stream and a slow history:
 
+
+
 - Fast stream: causal local attention over 512 or 1024 rows; retain per-row outputs.
+
 - Slow stream: summarize each COMPLETED32-row block from input embeddings, using
+
   pooled and last-row information, then apply a smaller causal Transformer over
+
   the at-most 625 completed blocks in a 20k sequence.
+
 - Every fourth fast block may cross-attend to slow history. A row at position t
+
   can see a slow token only when that token's block end is <=t. Slow self-attention
+
   is causal. Build summaries from input embeddings, not from later fast states
+
   that themselves depend on the slow branch; avoid a circular state definition.
+
 - No row earlier in a block may see its whole-block summary. At the completion
+
   row, that summary may include the current row. Define zero-length history,
+
   partial blocks, positions and sequence reset explicitly.
 
+
+
 This preserves an exact high-resolution recent path and a compressed older path.
+
 It changes the model and may discard useful older detail; compare it against the
+
 dense reference and measure age/activity regimes. The slow branch and cross
+
 projections add parameters beyond the trunk table below. Plain completed-block
+
 pooling before a per-row prediction without visibility masks would leak future.
 
+
+
 Use FP32 math SDPA as a correctness reference. Profile an explicitly IEEE-FP32
+
 FlexAttention/Triton implementation with forward AND backward checks for the
+
 selected masks, shapes and PyTorch build. Current FlexAttention/FA4 documentation
+
 does not certify that every backend supports our dtype and gradient path. Record
+
 the actual selected backend and dtype. Avoid materializing dense 20k masks for a
+
 sparse design. Activation checkpointing reduces retained activations, not the
+
 quadratic work of dense full attention. A GQA variant may reduce KV cost, but
+
 full MHA is the quality reference and GQA does not eliminate attention pair work.
 
+
+
 Full20k dense attention remains a legitimate teacher arm if a verified tiled
+
 FP32 kernel and real profile make it economical. Do not assume a sparse or
+
 compressed teacher is equivalent to full-history exact attention.

 ## Training signals that reward dynamics
 
+
+
 Use supervised regression as the main anchor. A proposed explicit target policy
+
 is c(y)=clip(y,-2,2), weight 0.05+abs(c(y)), and a separately normalized weighted
+
 mean squared error for each target. The0.05 floor and training clipping are
+
 recipe choices, not the official metric definition. Reuse the successful canonical
+
 target policy instead when doing a faithful baseline comparison; do not change
+
 target treatment and attribute the result entirely to architecture.
 
+
+
 Add future-observation learning as a declared auxiliary arm:
 
+
+
 - Predict normalized observable changes x[t+h]-x[t] at h=1,4,16,64,256.
+
 - Predict whether selected feature groups update within those horizons. This
+
   provides a signal beyond copying persistent values; report no-change and
+
   change-conditioned errors to detect a trivial persistence solution.
+
 - Future values appear ONLY as fitting targets, never inside the input embedding,
+
   normalization, patch, memory token or augmentation available to output t.
+
 - Mask unavailable horizons, padding and cross-sequence targets. Fit all scales
+
   and event-balancing constants on fitting components only. For a selected crop,
+
   load a target-only future tail or mask its missing horizons explicitly.
+
 - Start with Huber auxiliary losses normalized over their valid elements and a
+
   fixed coefficient 0.05. Measure shared-backbone gradient contributions before
+
   the long fit; freeze the coefficient rather than silently rebalancing it later.
+
   Each head and horizon needs its own declared denominator.
 
+
+
 Initially train supervision plus the admitted auxiliary losses jointly. A
+
 pretrain-then-finetune sibling may use only each outer fold's fitting components,
+
 with fresh or reset optimizer state specified at the transition. Self-supervised
+
 training on the outer fold would expose that fold even without target labels.
+
 The all-data final teacher is a later production artifact, not a held-out score.
 
+
+
 The optional output AR head follows the old proposal: yhat[t]=a[t]yhat[t-1]+
+
 (1-a[t])u[t], a[t]<0.99, initial a=0.10, model feedback only. It can be evaluated
+
 with a verified differentiable affine scan without serial Transformer calls.
+
 Never feed true lagged competition targets; their future horizon is undisclosed.
+
 AR is an ablation, because persistence can also blur abrupt changes. Keep the
+
 plain head reference. Record carried-state truncation/optimizer staleness if
+
 training crosses cores with detached state.

 ## Scale and memory: what fits
 
+
+
 NVIDIA's DGX B300 specification lists 288 GB per GPU; the receiving operator must
+
 verify actual visible memory, exclusivity and NVLink topology. Eight devices do
+
 not make one 2.3-TB allocation under DDP: each rank holds a full model replica.
 
+
+
 | Trunk | Layers | Width | Heads | SwiGLU width | Trunk parameters | FP32 state arithmetic,12–16 bytes/parameter |
+
 |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+
 | Smaller reference | 16 | 1024 | 16 | 2816 | 205.5M | 2.47–3.29 GB |
+
 | Large reference | 24 | 1536 | 24 | 4096 | 679.5M | 8.15–10.87 GB |
+
 | First flagship | 32 | 2048 | 32 | 5632 | 1.644B | 19.73–26.31 GB |
+
 | Scale extension | 40 | 2560 | 40 | 6912 | 3.172B | 38.06–50.75 GB |
+
 | Further capacity arm | 48 | 3072 | 48 | 8192 | 5.436B | 65.23–86.97 GB |
 
+
+
 These are analytical trunk counts, 4Ld²+3Ld*d_ff, before input encoders, norms,
+
 heads, slow stream and cross projections. Full counts must come from the model.
+
 The low state figure counts FP32 weights/gradients/Muon momentum; the conservative
+
 high figure uses two optimizer moments. Neither is total peak memory or a fit
+
 certificate. Include orthogonalization workspace, DDP buckets, allocator reserve,
+
 temporary optimizer arrays, checkpoint/export buffers and activations. A gradient
+
 bucket view can avoid some duplication but must be measured.
 
+
+
 At one sequence,32 heads and 20k rows, a single FP32 dense score map costs 51.2 GB;
+
 at 24 heads it costs 38.4 GB. Backward and softmax temporaries add more. DDP does
+
 not divide this allocation by eight. Bigger batch/context, not parameter states
+
 alone, is likely the admission constraint for these scales. The executable
+
 [capacity calculator](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/blob/experiment/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/research/experiment_drafts/large-dynamics-teacher-b300-r2/capacity.py)
+
 prints these state/map formulas and conditional step-time tables; it does not
+
 estimate activation peaks or certify memory safety.
 
+
+
 Choose0.68B and 1.65B for the first real quality contrast. Retain3.17B when useful
+
 underfitting, a better objective or improved transfer offers a concrete reason.
+
 Do not reject scale from one noisy screen, but do not assume a 5B teacher will
+
 generalize better from the same correlated dataset. Hundreds of millions of rows
+
 are not hundreds of millions of independent regimes.

 ## Muon, AdamW and schedule
 
+
+
 Use Muon on an explicit allowlist of hidden attention/FFN matrices. Keep numeric
+
 input encoders, learned embeddings, task readouts, norm scales and biases in
+
 AdamW groups even when a parameter is 2D. Every trainable parameter belongs to
+
 exactly one group. Keep Q/K/V as separately defined matrices for orthogonalization;
+
 fusing them into a tall QKV matrix changes the Muon update geometry.
 
+
+
 | Setting | Proposed starting recipe, not a measured optimum |
+
 |---|---|
+
 | Muon convention | `match_rms_adamw`, shape factor 0.2*sqrt(max(rows,cols)) |
+
 | Base peak LR,0.68B | 1e-4; targeted alternatives 0.5× and 2× |
+
 | Base peak LR,1.65B | 7.5e-5; targeted alternatives 0.5× and 2× |
+
 | Base peak LR,3.17B | 5e-5 starting prior; retune rather than assume a law |
+
 | Momentum / Nesterov | 0.95 / true |
+
 | Orthogonalization | 5 Newton–Schulz iterations, all intermediates FP32 |
+
 | AdamW groups | same base LR initially, betas(0.9,0.95), epsilon 1e-8 |
+
 | Weight decay | 0.05 on backbone matrices;0.01 on input/readout matrices;0 on biases/norms |
+
 | Clipping | global preclip norm logged, threshold 1.0, once per update before either optimizer |
+
 | Reference optimizer | AdamW on all matched groups, same base LR/schedule, separately declared contrast |
 
+
+
 The base LR above is NOT the original-Muon LR0.02 convention. Pin the shape
+
 adjustment; do not mix these recipes. In the referenced convention decay uses
+
 the unadjusted base LR; make that semantic explicit. Audit the installed source:
+
 current upstream PyTorch Muon casts Newton–Schulz work to BF16, so its unmodified
+
 implementation does not satisfy this plan. A source-pinned FP32 variant needs
+
 finite-update, dtype, state restoration and actual-step-cost checks. B300's
+
 advertised low-precision throughput is not available merely by using Muon.
 
+
+
 Use WSD for an extendable quality branch. Anchor warmup at 1500 successful updates
+
 for the initial 24-epoch,65,536-new-row/update scenario below. Use that SAME warmup
+
 for the 12/24/48-epoch descendants; this retains a shared stable prefix. For each
+
 frozen horizon branch from the stable checkpoint at 80% of that horizon, then
+
 cosine-decay over the final 20% to 0.1× peak. Preserve the uncooled stable state for
+
 an admitted extension. A cosine-only schedule at matched horizon is a separate
+
 comparison; neither scheduler is established as best for this task.
 
+
+
 Advance both optimizers and scheduler exactly once per successful update. Save
+
 loss components, LR per group, preclip norms, clipping/nonfinite counts, update
+
 norms, throughput and checkpoint identities. Never select the best outer-fold
+
 epoch retrospectively and present it as a fixed terminal comparison. EMA/SWA
+
 of cooled checkpoints is a declared candidate and must be evaluated, not an
+
 assumed gain. Warmup and LR must be rebudgeted if global batch changes.
 
+
+
 ## Eight-card execution
 
+
+
 Begin with ordinary synchronous NCCL DDP, one process per device. Model states
+
 at these scales are plausibly far below per-card capacity; DDP is for throughput,
+
 not pooling HBM. Compare one 8-rank job with two 4-rank jobs at the SAME global
+
 row batch and objective. Independent4-rank fits may deliver more useful completed
+
 comparisons; use measured time-to-graded-endpoint, not utilization percentage.
 
+
+
 For the 4096-window/2048-core reference,8 ranks ×2 windows/rank ×2 accumulation
+
 microsteps =65,536 NEW core rows/update, before boundary masks. The processed
+
 input count is about twice the new-row count because prefix is recomputed.
+
 With4 ranks use 4 windows/rank and 2 microsteps for the same nominal batch, subject
+
 to an actual profile. Whole20k-sequence training at 1 sequence/rank on 8 ranks
+
 instead gives about 160k raw rows/update and a different masked eligible count;
+
 do not reuse the 65,536-step/LR arithmetic for it.
 
+
+
 For target k and update window, let W_k be the all-reduced sum of fitting weights
+
 over ALL ranks and accumulation microsteps. Each rank's microstep loss is
+
 R/2 * sum_k(local_weighted_error_sum_k / W_k), under default DDP gradient averaging.
+
 Accumulate those terms without another division by accumulation count. Determine
+
 denominators from data/masks without retaining every forward graph. Normalize
+
 auxiliary objectives separately. `no_sync` encloses forward AND backward for
+
 nonfinal microsteps. Handle zero denominators coherently across ranks.
 
+
+
 Keep each live sequence on one rank where recurrent/slow state is used; reset
+
 all state, positions and feature priors correctly. Avoid sampler duplication;
+
 use zero-weight padded work to equalize collective counts when necessary. Compute
+
 the official score from pooled sufficient statistics or aligned prediction banks,
+
 not an average of rank correlations. Save RNG/sampler/sequence offsets as well
+
 as model, optimizer and scheduler states.
 
+
+
 Use pinned software and bounded resident data staging. Do not reread/decompress
+
 Parquet every microstep or copy all data once per rank. Compile fixed-shape work
+
 after correctness checks and report compile time separately. First use replicated
+
 Muon for a simple exact reference. If its orthogonalization is a measured
+
 bottleneck, an owner-per-WHOLE-matrix implementation can distribute that work
+
 and broadcast identical updates; splitting a matrix into arbitrary shards changes
+
 Muon. FSDP needs complete-matrix handling before orthogonalization and is not a
+
 free drop-in replacement. None of this optimizer-distribution code is implemented
+
 by this design packet.
 
+
+
 The supplied [gradient-delay paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30634) concerns
+
 asynchronous pipeline training and Muon's robustness to one-step delay. It does
+
 not establish a quality gain for synchronous DDP on this regression problem.
+
 Pipeline parallelism and error-feedback updates are a future engineering branch
+
 if a much larger model genuinely needs stages; they are not prerequisites for
+
 the first 1.65B teacher, whose state fits analytically on a single replica.
 
+

+

+

+

+# Research value loop and fresh reframe — 2026-10-18
+
+## Decision question
+
+The user clarified that a public submission is a confirmation of transfer, not
+the research objective. The objective remains improving the expected score of
+our strongest complete, deterministic endpoint under the unchanged
+`global_wp_clip2_v1` metric. Local component and training-seed evidence drives
+which model or mixture we prepare; a public score checks whether that direction
+transfers.
+
+The useful unit of research is a **decision changed by evidence per expensive
+GPU-hour**. GPU utilization by itself is not progress. A fit earns its cost when
+it answers a frozen comparison, preserves enough per-run evidence to diagnose
+why it moved, and has a clear route into the final teacher, student, or served
+mixture.
+
+## What we need to earn a larger score
+
+1. **A measurable source of edge.** Each experiment should isolate one mechanism
+   with an exact control, causal inputs, source-qualified fitting membership,
+   and the official scorer. This distinguishes useful signal from leakage,
+   evaluation noise, and model capacity.
+2. **Evidence that survives training and evaluation variation.** Keep the
+   registered paired seed/fold comparisons, report fold-level and per-seed
+   effects, and resample connected components separately. Existing folds are
+   exposed development evidence; more seeds do not make them pristine.
+3. **A complete-endpoint contribution.** A stronger teacher, a useful feature,
+   or a better student is an intermediate. Measure the resulting deterministic
+   student or fixed blend against its matched complete endpoint. Do not infer
+   that effects add, or that a better research-only model is already a better
+   submission.
+4. **Serving evidence before release.** Check causal state reset, exact
+   preprocessing parity, runtime, size and deterministic output under the
+   competition callback. A research feature without a streaming implementation
+   is evidence to invest in that path, not a package candidate.
+5. **One transfer check at the right time.** After local evidence supports an
+   endpoint, submit it to see whether the public slice agrees with the local
+   ranking. A mismatch is a research question; it is not a reason to tune to
+   leaderboard noise or to add a local delta to a public score.
+
+Use CPU for bounded data audits, sequence summaries, source and recipe checks,
+and score aggregation. Use GPU for paired learned comparisons whose outcome
+could change architecture, feature or distillation choices. Prefer streaming
+over staging every sequence into a multi-hundred-gigabyte feature array. Keep
+failed fits, ambiguous comparisons and negative controls in the evidence trail;
+they improve the next allocation even when they do not improve the score.
+
+## Current high-information work
+
+The current highest-value spend is the registered R4 comparison: 30 matched
+H512×1 GRU pairs across four component folds, with the 60-channel
+geometry/discrete suffix present versus zeroed. It directly asks whether the
+features that showed conditional signal in tiny pilots remain learnable at a
+much stronger from-scratch capacity. It does **not** test a teacher/student
+interaction, serving parity, or improvement over the strongest complete local
+endpoint.
+
+Evidence motivating R4 is deliberately mixed. The R1 moment pilot's pooled
+gain was opposed across exposed folds. The tiny R2 screen found heterogeneous
+effects and harmful naive concatenation in some arms. R3's three-seed H128×2
+screen put the all-feature arm below control, while a fixed half control /
+dictionary mixture was higher on only 46 evaluation sequences. These results
+justify the scale test; they do not establish a universal feature effect or
+reject the family. R4 is fixed to run all 30 pairs even if early scores look
+weak. Interpret the result at its actual scope:
+
+- A positive R4 result supports a stronger follow-up that tests the features
+  inside a useful teacher/student or complete-endpoint path; it is not by itself
+  submission evidence.
+- A mixed or imprecise result should guide a targeted representation,
+  interaction, or replication question. An interval crossing zero alone does
+  not close the direction.
+- A consistently negative result can defer this exact standalone concatenated
+  H512 recipe while preserving possible value in a teacher, student target,
+  residual, gate, or fixed mixture.
+
+All four folds are exposed or potentially exposed. The 30-pair result can
+support a strong local development comparison, but not a pristine holdout or a
+public score forecast. The running recipe and its admission status are tracked
+in the [R4 validation note](../validation/GEOMETRY_FROM_SCRATCH_R4_20261017.md).
+
+## Fresh proposals after repository overlap checks
+
+The independent reframe proposed five literature-inspired directions. Its
+priors were unknown and its first pass did not inspect this repository, so each
+idea was checked against existing work before allocation.
+
+| Proposal | Literature analogy | Existing overlap and next useful question |
+|---|---|---|
+| Lagged cross-instrument information (`i1` to `i0`) | Hasbrouck's trade/quote VAR and Cont et al.'s order-flow imbalance work ([Hasbrouck](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1991.tb03749.x), [Cont et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.6402)) | Not a new family: E-334's DTW lead/lag ridge was about −0.00008; E-415 proxy and shifted controls did not improve the unchanged backbone; E435 already proposed an `i0`-lag / shifted-`i1` control. Reopen only with a materially different lag representation or conditioning mechanism and a new placebo. |
+| Causal per-sequence normalization | RevIN studies instance normalization under time-series shift ([ICLR paper](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=cGDAkQo1C0p)) | The causal prefix-only adaptation is already in [Learning Round 1](../../campaign_2026-10-17/research_reset_r1/sources/LEARNING_ROUND1.md). First use the existing raw-data summaries to show that warm-up statistics predict later feature drift; full-sequence RevIN statistics would violate causality. |
+| Filtered regime-dependent predictors | Hamilton's switching-regression model ([paper](https://doi.org/10.2307/1912559)) | Overlaps the state/regime proposals in [Microstructure Round 1](../../campaign_2026-10-17/research_reset_r1/sources/MICROSTRUCTURE_ROUND1.md). A useful new arm would need a causal filter, an input-only gate, and a matched complexity control. |
+| Metric-aligned loss | Weighted prediction objectives | `wmse` is already the default R4 loss and uses the current metric's target-magnitude weighting. Re-deriving the score is worthwhile; spending on the same weighting is not a distinct experiment. |
+| Predictive self-supervision | Contrastive Predictive Coding ([CPC](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03748)) | Masked input reconstruction is already proposed in [Learning Round 1](../../campaign_2026-10-17/research_reset_r1/sources/LEARNING_ROUND1.md). Input prediction alone is not a score result; a paired target probe and an ancestry-clean student comparison would be required before scaling it. |
+
+These proposals remain eligible as descendants when they add a different
+mechanism and a control that changes the decision. The overlap review is a
+portfolio ordering decision, not a claim that the underlying families are
+false.
+
+## Research allocation rule
+
+For each GPU job, write down before launch:
+
+- the decision it can change and which teacher, student, or teacher/student
+  relationship it belongs to;
+- the exact strongest matched control, fitting ancestry, input/label timing,
+  metric, checkpoint and component membership;
+- the full resource envelope and what artifacts survive interruption;
+- the practical success case, an uncertain case and the recipe-specific
+  negative case; and
+- the next branch of work for each of those outcomes.
+
+This keeps the campaign moving without requiring an early score to beat the
+current system. The immediate use of compute is to finish R4 cleanly, then spend
+follow-up GPU time on the result's most informative interaction with a teacher,
+student or complete endpoint. The public submission comes after local ranking
+and serves only as a transfer check.
+
+## Provenance and evidence limits
+
+- Based on the user-directed local geometry campaign, R1–R3 records, the
+  independent read-only reframe proposal, repository overlap checks and the
+  independent R4 runner audit.
+- Literature links support analogies only; they provide no Wunder score prior.
+- All numerical local results cited above are exposed, small-panel evidence.
+- No new fit, submission or public score is claimed by this note.
