+# Teacher quality first: an empirical scaling programme
+
+## Question and latest instruction
+
+The user now prioritizes progressively stronger teachers. Distillation is optional
+future engineering, not a criterion for selecting, training or promoting a teacher.
+This amendment supersedes that strategic part of the earlier large-teacher design;
+its architecture descriptions and frozen proposal history remain useful.
+No experiment is admitted here. The B300 trainer is still unimplemented. Existing
+local start/budget, strict FP32 and stopped-controller restrictions remain binding.
+
+Goal: find the best held-out official prediction quality obtainable from permitted
+data and allocated compute. Estimate the marginal value of additional parameters,
+training, history and dynamics supervision before committing most server time.
+
+## Sources and what transfers
+
+Primary abstracts inspected on October 19 using web retrieval; no full-paper
+replication or arXiv helper invocation is claimed in this amendment.
+
+- [Chinchilla, 2203.15556](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15556): balance model size and
+  training data under a compute budget. Its language-token ratios and exponents
+  are not constants for our rows, objectives or correlated sequences.
+- [Data-constrained scaling, 2305.16264](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16264): repeated
+  data can help, with diminishing returns. Its observed repetition behaviour is
+  external LLM evidence, not our epoch recommendation.
+- [Time-series scaling, 2405.13867](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13867): decoder-only
+  forecasting models show scaling across a heterogeneous corpus. This motivates
+  measurement, but does not establish scaling on this small supplied corpus.
+- [Forecasting scaling and look-back, 2405.15124](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15124):
+  context length and granularity affect the scaling picture; longer history can
+  hurt. History is a separate axis from parameter count.
+- [Tensor Programs V, 2203.03466](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.03466): parameterization
+  can stabilize hyperparameter transfer across width. This is not proof that
+  standard muP rules transfer unchanged to Muon or simultaneous depth changes.
+
+See the [prior source register](../sources/TRANSFORMER_B300_SCALE_SOURCES_20261019_R2.md)
+for TradeFM, Muon internals, hardware, attention and the asynchronous pipeline paper.
+
+## What we actually measure
+
+Keep separate coordinates:
+
+- N: actual trainable parameters, plus trunk/head counts and architecture.
+- D: distinct fitting rows, sequences and source-qualified dependency components.
+- T: cumulative supervised core-row presentations; T/D records reuse, not new data.
+- I: processed input rows including repeated left context and auxiliary tails.
+- K: causally visible history; distinguish dense context, slow-memory summaries,
+  forward state and gradient horizon. They are not interchangeable.
+- C: measured GPU-seconds on the same device allocation; also record wall time,
+  per-update phases, peak memory, communication and a documented FLOP estimate.
+- U: successful updates, actual global core-row batch and independent component
+  count per update. Eight devices do not require an eightfold larger global batch.
+
+One time step with 112 columns is not 112 independent language tokens. Overlapping
+windows, repeated prefixes and epochs do not multiply independent information.
+A learned tokenizer changes attention cost and must retain a declared raw-row
+accounting. Unique component counts are essential even when raw row counts are huge.
+
+The often-used C approximately 6*N*T is only a dense matrix-work proxy here. It
+omits repeated context, attention score work, Muon orthogonalization, auxiliary
+heads, recomputation and communication. Use I and measured phases for estimates;
+never infer B300 wall time from an advertised low-precision FLOP rate.
+
+## Scaling design: learn a frontier before a law
+
+Freeze one causal backbone, objective, encoding, data membership, context and
+checkpoint policy. Initial ladder uses the existing trunk specifications:
+
+| Approximate trunk parameters | Layers | Width | FF width | Role |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
+| 0.206B | 16 | 1024 | 2816 | optimization and data-reuse anchor |
+| 0.679B | 24 | 1536 | 4096 | medium teacher |
+| 1.644B | 32 | 2048 | 5632 | first large teacher |
+| 3.172B | 40 | 2560 | 6912 | subsequent extension if informative |
+
+These change width and depth together: conclusions concern scale RECIPES, not a
+pure parameter-count causal effect. Input/readout parameters are additional.
+Keep head dimension 64 and SwiGLU initially. Do not fill 288 GB just because it is
+available. Allow 3B+ if its validation trajectory and optimization support it.
+
+**Proposed replacement first capacity panel: six total new fits**, three sizes
+0.206/0.679/1.644B times two matched fold/seed cells. Reuse the previously proposed
+F0/1001 and F2/1002 identities only after verifying ownership and clean ancestry.
+With two cells neither seed variance nor a scaling exponent is well identified.
+This proposal extends the old four-fit capacity panel; it does not authorize both
+panels. Before launch amend the machine recipe explicitly, bind sources and budget,
+and label the old recipe superseded. The event-objective panel remains separate.
+
+Save resumable stable-prefix checkpoints and predictions at predeclared budgets,
+for example 1/2/4/8/12 fitting passes, subject to measured cost. Evaluate larger
+models after sufficient optimization; a weak first epoch is not a scale verdict.
+There are two legitimate comparisons:
+
+1. Equal T/D: same fitting-row presentations and membership, revealing scale at
+   a fixed data-reuse budget while compute differs.
+2. Equal measured C: compare learning curves at overlapping GPU-hour budgets,
+   revealing the best quality for the available compute. Larger models see fewer
+   updates/rows at that budget; report that fact rather than hiding it.
+
+For WSD, a stable-prefix snapshot and a cooled terminal model are different
+endpoints. Use stable-prefix curves consistently; a cooled fork at an early budget
+requires its own recorded extra updates/GPU-hours. Such forks share ancestry, are
+not independent fits/replications, and must be listed as extra training work.
+Never compare a cooled small model to an uncooled large model without labeling it.
+
+After the initial panel, choose ONE informative 4-fit follow-up: size contrast,
+training length, context, or objective. It is separately allocated, not hidden in
+the six-fit screen. Keep exposed folds labeled exposed; no newly pristine holdout
+is created by larger models, another seed or server execution.
+
+## How to estimate scaling without fooling ourselves
+
+Start with learning curves and a Pareto table of official WP against GPU-hours,
+model size and reuse. Primary utility is the unchanged global_wp_clip2_v1; report
+per-target, component and sequence-position behaviour and matched differences.
+Track a fixed supervised validation loss separately from auxiliary NLL. Improving
+next-event likelihood alone is not evidence of better competition predictions.
+
+A possible later descriptive loss model is
+
+    L(N, D, R) = L_floor + A*N^(-alpha) + B*D_eff(D,R)^(-beta)
+    D_eff(D,R) = D * [1 + rho*(1 - exp(-(R-1)/rho))], R >= 1.
+
+This is a proposed saturation parameterization, not a fitted or validated law.
+Repeated rows still supply optimization exposure; D_eff is a fitted proxy, never
+an asserted count of independent samples. At fixed D the repetition scale rho
+is not identifiable from a few endpoints. Context and objectives require separate
+strata or much richer designs. Do not jointly fit floor/alpha/beta/rho from six
+fits and report a confident optimum. Checkpoint points share a trajectory and do
+not increase the number of independent fits.
+
+Use later evidence across several sizes, fitting-component fractions and budgets
+to compare a power law with a simple monotone/saturating alternative. Weight and
+resample at dependency-component level, report fitting-seed variation separately,
+and assess forecasts on a subsequently allocated size/budget. Initially extrapolate
+at most one size/budget rung. Do not translate a fitted loss delta into a public
+score, or assume official correlation utility obeys a power law.
+
+Data-scaling follow-up can compare 25/50/100 percent of fitting COMPONENTS with
+entire sequences retained. Use nested membership, matched clocks and controls;
+fractions change distribution as well as size. Adding valid.parquet to final
+all-data fitting removes its held-out interpretation. No extra external market
+data or synthetic-data benefit is assumed.
+
+## Parameters to tune, in priority order
+
+| Priority | Axis | Initial candidates | Interpretation |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | LR and parameter update scale | Muon base 0.5/1/2 times 7.5e-5; head AdamW LR independently recorded | rule out an optimization-limited large model |
+| 2 | Capacity versus reuse | ladder above; predeclared learning-curve budgets | locate compute frontier |
+| 3 | Context | 1024 vs 4096 initially; 8192/full-sequence slow memory later | test useful long-history signal |
+| 4 | Dynamics objective | coefficient 0 vs 0.05; event horizon 64 fixed | teach predictive dynamics without confounding size |
+| 5 | Numeric encoding | raw/group encoder vs raw plus numerical embeddings | help continuous value and cross-group reasoning |
+| 6 | Generalization | AdamW decay 0.01 vs 0.1; dropout 0 vs 0.05 when indicated | address observed train/validation divergence |
+| 7 | Shape/attention | matched-parameter depth/width, FF ratio, QK norm or gated attention | tune after signal and stable scale exist |
+
+Candidates are a menu for successive bounded panels, NOT a Cartesian sweep or
+an assertion all will run. Muon uses match_rms_adamw convention; original Muon
+LR 0.02 is not interchangeable with these bases. Norm/bias/embedding/readout groups
+remain explicit. Strict FP32 requires auditing the Newton-Schulz internals.
+
+Recommended optimization starting point: Muon momentum 0.95, five orthogonalization
+iterations, global clipping 1; AdamW betas (0.9,0.95), eps 1e-8 on remaining groups.
+Retain already frozen optimizer settings when reusing an existing control. Changing
+them creates a new recipe. Log groupwise update/weight RMS, preclip norm, clipping
+frequency, nonfinite events, activation RMS and attention entropy at bounded
+frequency. Diagnose large norms and frequent clipping before changing capacity.
+
+Use WSD as the extensible default: warmup approximately 5 percent of the declared
+initial update budget, stable prefix, final 20 percent cooldown. Freeze integer
+boundaries and ending LR before fitting; the old 1500-update warmup is not suitable
+for every short diagnostic. Compare cosine only in a separate schedule panel.
+Checkpoint-averaged endpoints are cheap to evaluate but require predeclared weight
+averaging windows and cannot be counted as independent models.
+
+Start from the prior nominal 65,536 new core rows/update only if a real-shape
+profile supports it; it is not an optimum. Screen half that batch if optimization
+or component diversity suggests it. Change accumulation to preserve global batch
+when comparing 4-way with 8-way DDP. Optimize completed comparable fits/hour, and
+choose 8-way for an individual large fit only when measured scaling justifies it.
+muP is a possible later width-transfer method, not a guarantee for this Muon recipe;
+do not introduce muP and a new optimizer simultaneously into the scale control.
+
+## What the observations would mean
+
+- Larger train AND validation improve, with usable slope: extend capacity/compute.
+- Larger train improves but validation worsens: investigate reuse, component
+  diversity, regularization and objectives; do not simply add more epochs.
+- Larger train is worse: investigate optimization/update scale and sufficient
+  updates before interpreting it as a statistical capacity limit.
+- Long context hurts: check masks, effective row budget, prefix cost and optimization;
+  compare useful memory at matched compute before rejecting long-range dynamics.
+- Auxiliary loss improves but official utility is flat: representation changed,
+  yet target relevance is unproven; measure target effects and reduce its weight.
+- Predictive signal improves at higher cost: retain the quality endpoint and Pareto
+  tradeoff. No GRU-transfer gate is required by the latest teacher-first objective.
+

+screen according to the measured blocker. Receiver must declare a server GPU-hour

+# Build the next candidate through teacher-to-student transfer
+
+## Question and hypothesis
+
+Can causal state features add value inside teacher training and then transfer into one compact, deterministic GRU student more effectively than combining the teacher predictions at inference?
+
+**Hypothesis:** retaining the raw input path while adding one causal learned state representation to a source-qualified teacher may improve the student target. A student that absorbs complementary information during training could preserve a useful fraction of it without deploying another full model or relying on a validation-selected ensemble coefficient.
+
+## Why this is the best supported combination direction so far
+
+The completed model-space mixture evidence is consistently unfavorable for the specific TL3/R3 pair. On exposed F0, TL3 scored 0.701818 WP, compared with 0.698202 for fixed 75/25 and 0.693740 for fixed 50/50. On exposed F2, TL3 scored 0.723887, compared with 0.722678 and 0.720950. The F2 paired component intervals for both mixtures versus TL3 were wholly negative. An input-only warmup router also lost to its parent on all four folds, and the causal lagged-pseudo-label gate added only +0.00004795 over the fixed blend with a zero-crossing interval. These results argue against making another TL3/R3 mixture from the same exposed cache.
+
+They do not show that all ensembles or teachers are useless. They show that this R3 member is not demonstrated to improve the served TL3 endpoint through fixed output averaging or the tested gates. The more defensible integration point is the training target/representation, where a teacher may impart conditional information to a student even when it is a weaker standalone predictor.
+
+## Proposed candidate construction after explicit resumption
+
+1. **Anchor the deliverable.** Keep the strongest publicly confirmed package as the serving reference. The user reports a public team best of 0.66832; the exact archive and ancestry must be recorded before using it as a clean-fold source. Do not infer a public score by adding a local delta.
+2. **Use source-clean teacher predictions.** For research comparison, create per-cell teachers with fitting membership excluding each evaluated component. Treat the existing TL3 ZIP as a submission/reference endpoint until its teacher and initializer ancestry are verified; do not silently use possibly all-data predictions as held-out targets.
+3. **Add one causal representation at a time.** Start from an existing published causal-state handoff, especially [PR #17](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/17), which already specifies raw-retaining local-trend teacher arms and matched standard-GRU student-cache replacement. Treat the innovation-conditioned local draft and [predictive-state PR #18](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/18) as separate, not stacked, targets until each has profile, clean source registry and teacher evidence.
+4. **Compare complete student endpoints.** Keep an ordinary-cache student control and replace exactly one predeclared teacher family for each treatment. Match student architecture, fitting membership, seed, target scale, cache coefficient, schedule, checkpoint rule and serving conversion. A component can pay off through student quality even if its teacher score is lower; grade the student itself.
+5. **Use checkpoint averaging as a separate, low-serving-cost arm.** Existing [PR #13](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/13) covers averaging checkpoints from one trajectory. Compare it after freezing the training recipe; do not confuse it with averaging unrelated seeds or teachers.
+6. **Package only the frozen winner.** Compare the fixed student against the best reference with source-qualified cross-fold and seed evidence, then run exact-package deterministic CPU and size/runtime checks. Preserve public feedback as transfer evidence, not coefficient-selection feedback.
+
+## What not to combine from the present evidence
+
+- Do not average R3 geometry output with TL3 at 25% or 50%; both tested weights lose on two exposed panels. A new coefficient fitted on these panels would be adaptive and would not create clean evidence.
+- Do not append the 39 groupwise Kalman statistics directly to a ridge/feature vector: that exact proxy lost by −0.013093 WP on nonofficial train rows. The two recurrent follow-ups changed sign across seeds and do not show stable gain.
+- Do not route experts from the first 99 rows with the tested warmup gate; it underperformed. Do not treat the previous-row-label proxy as mature test-time feedback.
+- Do not stack all geometry, moments, dictionary, clock and latent-observer features into one unidentifiable mega-arm. Use matched controls and explicit interaction nodes so an endpoint change remains interpretable.
+
+## Current status
+
+This is a proposal formed from existing records only. It does not admit a fit, score, blend export, package, upload or PR. The user's stop at 2026-10-18 08:27 UTC remains authoritative. Both geometry ZIPs were already submitted according to the user; they are not candidates to repeat. Existing published PRs cover the large causal-state, predictive-state, and trajectory-averaging ideas. The local innovation-gain code branch is unpushed and has no B300 evidence.
+
+## Cheapest discriminating study once reopened
+
+Reuse PR #17's matched teacher/student route rather than creating a new campaign. First bind a clean per-cell teacher registry and pass the actual-device profile and causal/reset checks. Then compare the ordinary cache against exactly one causal teacher replacement in paired fold/seed cells. Promote only when the standard-GRU student endpoint improves with stable evidence, and separately report the teacher score, student score, runtime, archive size and ancestry. All current folds are exposed, so a fresh source-qualified or prospective confirmation is still required for transfer claims.

+# Warmup-only routing among related experts
+
+## Question or claim
+
+Do summaries from a sequence's first 99 input rows predict which of four existing endpoints will be strongest later in that sequence?
+
+## Mechanism and method
+
+A standardized ridge gate used mean, log standard deviation and normalized early-to-late drift for 13 input groups. It was trained on per-sequence official scores for four source-qualified F0 experts, with component-grouped four-fold cross-fitting. The frozen recipe and full implementation record are in the [campaign packet](../../campaign_2026-10-18/online_features_r1/warmup_expert_gate_r1/README.md).
+
+## Evidence and interpretation
+
+On 468 repeatedly inspected F0 groups/141 components, the gate scored 0.680833 WP versus 0.681227 for the training-selected fixed parent and 0.680826 for an equal mixture. It lost to the fixed parent in all four held-out component folds. The paired component interval for gate minus fixed parent was [−0.000748, −0.000088], conditional on fitted cross-fit gates. Input-dependent weight dispersion was 0.0121–0.0173 across folds, below the preregistered 0.10 threshold in every fold. The gate stayed near equal weights.
+
+## Limits and validity
+
+All candidate endpoints and labels had prior F0 exposure. Cross-fitting prevents within-screen gate label reuse, not validation exposure, selection, seed or transfer bias. This result narrows this warmup-summary router over these four related experts. It does not falsify richer online adaptation, actual matured feedback, Kalman state features, or teacher/student transfer.
+
+## Decision and next step
+
+The predeclared B300 admission rule failed on all three criteria, so no new B300 draft was created for this router. The existing retained-raw Kalman teacher/student direction remains in [draft PR #17](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/17). Broader online-learning work remains open; any new large-scale handoff needs a distinct mechanism and local evidence that can change the decision.

+# Local train Parquet metadata OOM, 2026-10-18
+
+## Status
+
+Contained to one 1 GB transient systemd scope. The feature-only feasibility
+screen is stopped; no retry or further Parquet read is authorized by this
+receipt. This is an operational failure, not scientific evidence for or
+against the innovation-clock idea.
+
+## Attempt and impact
+
+At 2026-10-18 06:07:59 Europe/Kyiv, a bounded Python command attempted to
+inspect row-group counts for `datasets/train.parquet` and then
+`datasets/valid.parquet`. The command began with `pyarrow.parquet.ParquetFile`
+on the 29,240,219,011-byte train file. It did not print output, did not reach
+the validation file, and did not read a row group. No output file was written.
+The command requested 1 CPU, 1,000,000,000 bytes of memory, zero swap, and a
+120-second runtime through `scripts/limited`; scratch pointed at the approved
+physical `research_tmp` filesystem.
+
+At 06:08:00 the kernel OOM-killed Python inside
+`run-p3081242-i3058961.scope`. `systemd` reports `Result=oom-kill`,
+`MemoryMax=1,000,000,000`, `MemoryPeak=999,997,440`, `MemorySwapMax=0`, and
+668,198,000 ns CPU time. The kernel reports 974,228 KiB anonymous RSS at kill.
+This is a real child-scope OOM. The parent campaign slice's hierarchical
+`oom`/`oom_kill` counters moved from the prior recorded 3/3 to 4/4; its local
+counter remained 0/0. Do not describe this as “no OOM” merely because the
+desktop survived or the child had a memory cap.
+
+The failed operation attempted Parquet-footer metadata parsing only; it never
+selected targets, masks, or input row values. Immediately beforehand, a
+separate validation-only check successfully read the footer and `seq_ix` /
+`step_in_seq` from five validation row groups. That success did not establish a
+safe memory bound for the much larger train file.
+
+## Cause and prevention
+
+I assumed the train Parquet footer would be small without first measuring or
+bounding its metadata length. The file's payload size was known, but its
+row-group count and footer size were not. `ParquetFile` materialized unknown
+metadata under a hard cap, which contained the failure but did not prevent an
+OOM.
+
+Do not repeat a full `ParquetFile(train.parquet)` open from this screen. Any
+future train-file metadata inspection must first use a trusted producer
+manifest or a bounded footer-length read that rejects metadata above an
+explicit pre-admitted size. If no such bound is available, use existing
+source-qualified manifests and cached artifacts, or leave the screen
+unrun. Keep the task stopped until a safe metadata route is established.
+
+## Provenance
+
+- Campaign: [`online_features_r1`](../../campaign_2026-10-18/online_features_r1/README.md)
+- Scope: `run-p3081242-i3058961.scope`
+- Kernel event: `journalctl -k`, 2026-10-18 06:08:00 Europe/Kyiv,

+# Dynamics auxiliary FP32 window stability
+
+## Question or claim
+
+Does the FP32 target builder preserve small future input changes after a large earlier pulse? The original global-prefix calculation fails this synthetic check before any auxiliary profile or scientific fit.
+
+## Mechanism and method
+
+The target builder subtracted two long cumulative sums of squared changes. In the [original20000-row fixture](../../campaign_2026-10-21/next_cycle_r1/DYNAMICS_NUMERICAL_PROBE_R1.json), an early10000-unit pulse makes the accumulated sum too coarse to retain later0.01 transitions. Both16/256-step horizons at position16000 return−18.420681 instead of the direct-window−9.2102404:9.21044log-unit error.
+
+The repair keeps the original FP32 normalized inputs,13feature groups, output order, epsilon placement, and start/endpoint masks. Signed means use normalized endpoint differences. Energy uses per-transition group mean-square changes and positive block-local prefix/suffix sums, so no window subtracts a distant large prefix. The mathematical52-target definition and loss are unchanged; finite-precision arithmetic is intentionally corrected. Auxiliary heads and targets remain outside the causal prediction path and are stripped for serving.
+

+## Question or claim

+## Mechanism and method

Exact final row-group receipts and recursive teacher/initializer hashes remain unavailable. +A separate, modest i1 result is that raw/event i1 inputs matter more clearly than this history addition on the first cell. Yet the frozen 90%B/10%C mixture is +0.000360 [−0.0000119, +0.0007089]. This is consistent with a weak complementary contribution despite worse standalone C, but the interval does not establish a positive gain. It is not evidence that history is useless or that the readout is the bottleneck: a 91.35% head gradient-square share and 97.27% clip rate are optimization descriptions, not causal tests.
+
+## Limits and validity
+
+The host replay now scores the cached legacy endpoint at 0.7018181213 versus 0.7018175337 for the current-host reference, a −0.000000588 difference with a 95% component interval spanning zero. CP5 minus that same-host reference remains −0.007362916 [−0.009617579, −0.005574297]. This supersedes the earlier interim review's statement that a full current-host comparison was still pending, and falsifies a current-host runtime/replay mismatch as the material source of the measured replacement gap. It does not identify a dependency-specific cause for the earlier Docker/host prediction discrepancy, nor remove TL3 exposure or ancestry limitations.
+
+F0 was previously inspected. The native grade covers 468 sequences and 141 components; its conditional intervals do not measure training variation, clean-CV generalization or public transfer. The i1 grade is one F0/seed1001 cell from the predeclared six-fit screen, also on exposed development data. The near-zero lower endpoint of the 90/10 interval must not be presented as established improvement. The i1 labels A/B/C are unrelated to the endpoint-diagnosis symbols B/R/S.
+
+## Decision and next step
+
+For i1, the cheapest decision-changing evidence is the already-authorized F2/seed1002 A/B/C cell and the frozen full-panel grade. It adds no experiment beyond the six-fit panel and can show whether raw-input and fixed-mixture patterns recur across the second fold/seed. If those prediction artifacts have not landed, the current source and JSON cannot resolve that uncertainty; wait for them rather than add fits or tune coefficients.
+
+For H512, the existing same-host replay and cached-prediction geometry exhaust the useful no-fit checks here. Keep this result labeled as an exposed, exposure-asymmetric fixed-endpoint diagnostic. It cannot support an architecture ranking, a public-score prediction, or a claim that rescaling or another blend would improve the submission.

+# i1 and dynamics native-serving compatibility
+
+This source-only review traces the canonical checkpoint exporter and callback
+to check whether stripping the optional dynamics head makes the current
+367-input screen models directly packageable. It does not load model tensors,
+prediction or data arrays, run tests, or measure runtime. The review found a
+serving compatibility gap; it does not change the frozen cold-screen recipes
+or imply a model-quality result.
+
+[`package_submission.py`](../../../scripts/package_submission.py) converts the
+checkpoint state to FP32 and calls
+[`strip_dynamics_auxiliary_state`](../../../src/wnn/training/dynamics_auxiliary.py)
+before validating its input layout. That helper removes the 52-output head and
+two target-statistics buffers, but retains `mean`, `std`, `inp.weight`, and the
+checkpoint's declared `n_in`. The subsequent
+[`native_input_metadata`](../../../src/wnn/native_representation.py) accepts
+211 or 323 inputs in `none` mode and 467 in the named `base`/`ema` modes. It
+does not describe a 367-column `i1_history` layout. Consequently both active
+history C and the all-zero-history B control fail the canonical export gate;
+removing the auxiliary head does not repair their input width.
+
+The default package callback,
+[`solution_multi.PredictionModel`](../../../submission/solution_multi.py), is
+Python code but delegates feature construction and recurrent inference to
+`wnn_native.Predictor`. It passes each raw `data_point.state` row to that
+predictor and resets member state at a sequence change. Rust's
+[`Predictor`](../../../native/src/python.rs) accepts only raw width 112 at its
+row boundary, then constructs the 99 event columns and an optional supported
+suffix. Its current layouts cover 211/323 `none` inputs or 467 `base`/`ema`
+inputs; it has no 156-column i1-history builder. The separate
+[`StreamingI1History`](../../../src/wnn/i1_history_streaming.py) helper is not
+wired into this package callback. The lower-level Rust `ModelStepper` accepts
+precomputed model inputs of its weight-defined width, but does not turn the
+official 112-wide raw callback row into the complete 367-wide input. It is not
+an existing end-to-end serving path for these checkpoints.
+
+There is a source-supported projection path for the B-control representation.
+[`RNNModel._normalized_inputs`](../../../src/wnn/nn.py) applies the 367-wide
+normalization and then sets the masked history coordinates to exact zero before
+the input projection. For a checkpoint whose provenance confirms
+`research_features=i1_history`, `research_feature_control=all`, and
+`drop_i1=false`, the model's mathematical function can therefore be represented
+with the first 211 means/scales and first 211 `inp.weight` columns, preserving
+`inp.bias` and every other model tensor. The current exporter does not perform
+this projection, rewrite the exported width metadata, or record that
+transformation. This is a feasibility observation, not verified FP32/native
+parity. In practice, different matrix widths can change floating-point
+reduction order, so exact output identity must be measured rather than inferred
+from the algebra alone.
+
+Before using a projected B-control model in a complete endpoint, the narrow
+proof is to implement an explicitly gated export conversion for only that
+semantic mask; preserve original checkpoint and source hashes; assert the
+projected tensor shapes and unchanged bias/backbone; and compare the original
+masked 367-input model against the packaged callback over complete sequences
+with sequence-reset replay. The comparison must use the actual package
+`PredictionModel.predict` path, exact supported raw inputs, full row coverage,
+and an explicit numerical tolerance. Then measure the full package's runtime
+and size under the official serving harness. The existing cold-screen
+prediction grader does not establish any of those packaging or cost results.
+
+Active C cannot use that projection because its 156 history inputs affect the
+model. Supporting it requires a package input layout and causal feature
+streamer with the fitting-only history prior, reset/carry semantics, and parity
+against the frozen Python feature/model path, followed by a complete callback
+cost measurement. No such native or package integration is present in the
+reviewed source.
+
+The dynamics head is absent from ordinary evaluation outputs and can be
+removed from an exported state, so the auxiliary objective adds no required
+serving head. The stronger claim that these screen checkpoints already have a
+cheap, supported native endpoint is not established: the common 367-input
+representation is still rejected. For the all-zero-history control, a 211
+projection is a plausible low-cost route, but it remains unimplemented and
+unmeasured. This caveat does not change the accepted cold-fit plan, whose
+prediction and official-score stages run through the existing PyTorch path.
+
+The related [warm-parent catalog](STRONG_PARENT_F0_F1_WARM_INIT_CATALOG_20261022_R1.md)
+covers the distinct inheritance and normalization gates. This review makes no
+recommendation to select C, project a checkpoint, or admit follow-up fits.

+# Interpreting the i1 history standalone and fixed-mixture pattern
+
+## Question and scope
+
+Does the first F0 history contrast point to a useful representation contribution,
+or could the fixed-mixture result come from prediction-distribution and
+optimization effects? This is a read-only review of score and run metadata. I
+did not open prediction or target arrays, fit tensors, or run code. F0 is
+previously exposed development data; its component intervals condition on the
+three fitted models and do not measure training, fold, or public-transfer
+uncertainty.
+
+## What the first cell shows
+
+In the matched F0/seed1001 cell, B is the standard-input model without history;
+C adds the frozen history channels; A masks both the i1 inputs and history.
+C scores 0.655537 versus B at 0.659074, with C−B at −0.003537
+(95% paired-component interval [−0.007283, −0.000066]). Yet the predeclared
+`0.9*B + 0.1*C` endpoint is +0.000360 over B, with interval
+[−0.0000119, +0.0007089]. Its point deltas are positive for both targets and
+all four fixed position bins. The matching `0.9*B + 0.1*A` result is nearly
+flat at −0.000023, with an interval spanning zero. The bin values are point
+estimates only; no bin intervals were reported.
+
+This pattern is compatible with a weak complementary correction: C can be a
+worse full replacement while a small fixed contribution helps B. The contrast
+with A makes the C mixture more interesting than a candidate-agnostic averaging
+story. It still does not establish history complementarity. C−B is the clean
+history treatment, but a better fixed mixture can also arise because C changes
+prediction dispersion, clipping, or the optimizer's trajectory. F0 C's high
+head-gradient share and clipping rate are descriptions of that run, not
+evidence for a causal bottleneck.
+
+There is a useful constraint on the shrinkage explanation. The official score
+is a weighted Pearson correlation after clipping at ±2. A positive scalar
+rescaling of an unclipped prediction alone cannot change Pearson correlation.
+So a distribution-based explanation would need to change relative prediction
+structure or interact with clipping; it cannot be only “C shrinks B.” The F0
+summary does not report the clipped prediction fractions or covariance and
+variance terms needed to tell those cases apart.
+
+## What F2 can and cannot resolve
+
+The available F2/seed1002 B run scores 0.684108 (t0 0.683801, t1 0.684415)
+after 4,830 updates. That is a standalone fold-2 score, not a paired contrast;
+its absolute value should not be compared with F0 B. At review time, F2 A and C
+and the frozen mixture grade were still pending in the current run log. Until
+they land, this cell says nothing about whether the F0 pattern recurs.
+
+The frozen F2 A/B/C grade will provide the cheapest already-authorized
+cross-cell check: inspect C−B and the fixed `0.9*B + 0.1*C`−B deltas for both
+targets and the four fixed bins, alongside the A control. A recurring positive
+fixed-mixture delta while C remains weaker alone would strengthen the case for
+a useful small contribution. A null or negative mixture would leave the F0
+pattern unconfirmed, not falsify every history representation. F0/1001 and
+F2/1002 change both fold and seed, and both folds have prior exposure, so this
+two-cell screen cannot separate fold from seed variation or provide fresh
+confirmation.
+
+Scores and bins alone still cannot distinguish complementary information from
+distribution effects. If that distinction changes the next allocation, one
+no-fit calculation on the already-saved prediction caches can decompose the
+fixed mixture after the official clipping and label weighting. For each target
+and fixed bin, let `B_c = clip(B, ±2)`, `M_c = clip(0.9*B + 0.1*C, ±2)`, and
+`D = M_c - B_c`. Report the weighted covariance of `D` with the target and
+with the target residual after its best weighted affine projection on `B_c`,
+alongside the weighted variance terms and clipped fractions for B and M. A
+positive residual covariance in both cells would support a distinct corrective
+direction. A mixture change with little residual covariance but altered clipped
+fractions or variance geometry would favor a distribution/calibration account.
+This is diagnostic only: it uses exposed labels, adds no fit, and cannot prove
+that the representation rather than its treatment-specific optimization path
+caused the effect. No coefficient search is needed or proposed.
+
+## Limits and records
+
+The fixed C mixture's overall interval just crosses zero; the current F0 result
+is therefore suggestive, not an established blend gain. The component
+bootstrap addresses evaluation-unit variation conditional on fixed predictions,
+not fitted-model variation. The F2 B score has no matched A/C result yet. No
+public forecast or mechanism promotion follows.
+
+Sources: [F0 A/B/C interim grade](../../campaign_2026-10-21/next_cycle_r1/i1/interim_f0_abc/RESULT_R1.json),
+[current F2 run log](../../campaign_2026-10-21/next_cycle_r1/i1/runtime/panel_r2.log),
+[F2 B score record](../../../artifacts/runs/i1_f2_s1002_b_r1/score.json),
+[prior endpoint interpretation](H512_ENDPOINT_INTERPRETATION_REVIEW_20261021_R1.md),
+and the [accepted cycle plan](../../../specs/plans/2026-10-21-next-local-kaggle-cycle.md).
+
+## Source-based follow-up interpretation
+
+After the fixed geometry diagnostic, root proposed and dynamics_builder independently checked a narrower optimization explanation using source and metadata only. Both cold B and C have identical stored initial parameters and normalization. B masks the 156 appended inputs after normalization, while C activates their existing random, nonzero input-projection weights. Their effective initial functions therefore differ. The cold treatment changes history exposure and its resulting optimization path together; it does not change parameter count or establish a measured conditioning/variance effect.
+
+The [measured F0 geometry](../../campaign_2026-10-21/next_cycle_r1/i1/fixed_mix_geometry_r1/RESULT_R1.json) excludes clipping-only and pure scalar shrinkage accounts for its small positive point gain, while remaining conditional on the same exposed fits. It cannot determine whether the corrective direction arose from useful history information or the changed training trajectory. No added confidence interval or independent replication follows from this decomposition.
+
+The already conditional strong-parent comparison offers a useful falsifier. Extend both control and treatment to the same 367-slot input, initialize appended projection weights to zero, preserve the original 211 input statistics, use one explicit shared normalization choice for new slots, and verify identical parent predictions before fitting. Then only the treatment receives unmasked history inputs and their gradients. Failure to improve the paired strong controls or the fixed endpoint contribution would weaken the explanation that a cold initialization/short schedule obscured useful history. This is an interpretation of the existing four-fit follow-up, not another admitted panel or a changed cold recipe.
+
+The [warm-parent catalog](STRONG_PARENT_F0_F1_WARM_INIT_CATALOG_20261022_R1.md) records two necessary implementation gates: `none` to `i1_history` is currently rejected, and generic inheritance assigns new slots mean0/std1 while cold C fits their statistics. The separate 64-group i1 prior normalizes only the energy feature construction; it is not a replacement for those input statistics. Historical parent FP16/AMP and distinct initializer/cache ancestry remain explicit. Root still waits for the existing F2 cell before selecting a mechanism; no warm code or fits were added by this review.

+# Independent review of the completed i1 history screen
+
+The terminal grade supports a small, fixed 90/10 B/C mixture contribution on
+both tested cells. It does not support the history model as a standalone
+replacement, establish a history-specific mechanism, or qualify a submission.
+The two-cell consistency is enough to retain the already conditional four-fit
+strong-parent follow-up as a bounded research screen, provided its warm-start
+parity, exposure, and serving gaps remain explicit. Root owns fit admission and
+allocation.
+
+This review reads the committed grade JSON, frozen recipes, small source
+receipts, and source code only. I did not open prediction, target, or checkpoint
+arrays, run a grader or tests, load a model, or perform new fits. I did not
+independently regrade the fixed predictions.
+
+## Evidence and fixed comparison
+
+The six-fit screen compares A (all i1 inputs masked), B (history masked), and C
+(history active) on F0/seed1001 and F2/seed1002. Each arm has two fits, for six
+new fits total, with no teacher or reused-model fits. The saved grade reports
+468 F0 groups / 141 connected components and 443 F2 groups / 144 components;
+it records complete float32 prediction coverage and the fixed official
+`global_wp_clip2_v1` score. Its provenance checks require the common initial
+parameter and normalization identities within each cell, fixed epoch-2
+checkpoints, complete three-epoch update counts, exact fit/evaluation
+membership, and prediction sidecar/checkpoint correspondence.
+
+The screen's original grader already fixed the two mixtures at `0.9*B + 0.1*A`
+and `0.9*B + 0.1*C` before outcomes (`4078ae085`). The terminal grader does not
+search coefficients. The admission receipt pins the training source revision
+`b1b680d4a700d353f3e6db4f761f6670bd02fc7f`; source hashes for the trainer,
+predictor, feature construction, model/input, preprocessing, evaluator, and
+metric match that historical tree. The terminal grade's grader, scorer,
+evaluation, and metric hashes also match their recorded source files. The
+target cache is pinned by the grader to SHA-256
+`dbb7a1a48dd0af9fa524a80c2694008a56cb91d5dae80e8d0d4984c0c5622955`; this
+review did not read or hash that payload.
+
+| Cell | C − B | Fixed 90/10 B+C − B (95% component interval) | Fixed 90/10 B+A − B (95% component interval) |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|
+| F0 / seed 1001 | −0.003537 [−0.007283, −0.000066] | +0.00035953 [−0.00001187, +0.00070893] | −0.00002308 [−0.00030904, +0.00026620] |
+| F2 / seed 1002 | −0.003903 [−0.005818, −0.002287] | +0.00027145 [+0.00008223, +0.00043398] | +0.00054446 [+0.00031366, +0.00075637] |
+
+The unweighted mean of the two B/C mixture point deltas is `+0.00031549`.
+This is a descriptive two-cell average, not a pooled confidence estimate. B/C
+mixture deltas are positive for both targets in both cells: F0 `+0.00052218`
+and `+0.00019688`; F2 `+0.00037163` and `+0.00017128`. They are also positive
+in each of the four fixed position bins in both cells. Those target/bin values
+are point estimates without intervals and are correlated with the overall
+score, not separate replications.
+
+The uncertainty is conditional on the fitted predictions: 2,000 resamples of
+source-qualified connected components, seed 271828. F0's B/C mixture interval
+just crosses zero; F2's interval is positive. There is one fit per arm in each
+fold/seed cell, so these intervals do not quantify training variability. Fold
+and seed also change together. Both folds were previously inspected
+development data, not fresh confirmation. The grader reports no across-cell
+interval, and the bin/target point deltas do not add one.
+
+## Interpretation and follow-up value
+
+C loses to B alone in both cells, while the frozen B/C mixture is slightly
+positive. That pattern is compatible with a weak complementary correction, but
+the gain is small and not unique to history: the B/A mixture is flat on F0 and
+larger than B/C on F2. A fixed mixture can benefit from model diversity or
+prediction geometry without proving that the appended history carries a
+portable mechanism. The fact that all B/C target/bin point deltas are positive
+is encouraging consistency, not additional independent evidence.
+
+The cold A/B/C runs share an initial-parameter hash within each cell, but that
+does not mean they share the same initial function. C exposes nonzero randomly
+initialized projection weights on the appended history columns; B masks those
+inputs after normalization. The treatment therefore changes both history
+exposure and the effective initial function/optimization path. The cold screen
+cannot isolate those effects.
+
+The existing four-fit plan is a reasonable next bounded test of the warm-start
+question: one control and one history treatment in each of F0 and F1, compared
+within fold. Keep the fixed 90/10 endpoint and scoring contract frozen, verify
+that the zero-extended child reproduces its parent before any fit, and treat
+results as exposed development evidence. F0 and F1 parents have different
+ancestry and historical precision, so their deltas should not be pooled as
+independent replications. This screen warrants spending the existing
+conditional allocation to investigate a strong-parent contribution; it does
+not warrant promotion or an expected public-score claim.
+
+The warm code in `cc9af1c68745289a71e30aa45e5242af87a3f5bf` is default-off and
+narrows extension to a standard 211-input `none` parent and 367-input
+`i1_history` child. It zero-extends the input projection, retains the inherited
+211 means/scales, and has a `fit-appended` mode that fits only the extra 156
+normalization slots from the first two fitting-loader batches, retaining every
+seventh flattened row. The helper saves and restores the parent mean/std and
+checks their tensor identities. It rejects resume-state training and unsupported
+parent/input combinations. Source inspection supports these intended
+invariants, but it is not an initial-output parity measurement; preserve that as
+a pre-fit gate. The current warm provenance records the estimator and fit
+membership, not an identity for the exact two normalization batches.
+
+There is a sampler detail to freeze for this follow-up. With the known seeded
+`EpochOrderSampler`, normalization starts at epoch −1 and `prepare_epoch`
+resets it to epoch 0 before fitting. With `batch_order=random`, the loader uses
+shuffle and the normalization pass consumes the first two batches before epoch
+0, advancing its RNG state. The existing strong-parent recipes use random
+shuffle. If they remain the basis, the follow-up must either isolate/restore the
+sampler RNG around normalization or explicitly freeze this new order and record
+the sampled normalization batches. Do not describe it as the historical random
+order otherwise.
+
+There is also a packaging boundary: the existing native callback/export path
+does not accept the 367-column `i1_history` layout. The all-zero-history B form
+has a possible 211-column projection, but conversion and native parity are
+unimplemented; active C needs a history feature builder and state/reset path.
+Thus the measured PyTorch blend is not a currently packageable endpoint. Any
+four-fit result remains research evidence until the active-history native path
+or an explicitly supported conversion is implemented and evaluated.
+
+Finally, this review did not run tests. The root's reported broad compatibility
+run found one preexisting `test_fixed_checkpoints` failure: the test patches
+`train_rnn.market_class`, while `evaluate` resolves to
+`wnn.training.evaluation.evaluate`, which uses its own imported `market_class`.
+The warm commit changes neither that evaluator nor the failing test; the source
+diff from the preceding grade commit confirms the mismatch is outside the warm
+change. It is a test-fixture issue, not evidence against the completed grade.
+

+A standard parent has 112 raw plus 99 event inputs (211 total). `i1_history` appends 156 causal channels for a 367-input child. The current gate’s `appendable_modes` omits `I1_HISTORY_MODE`, so `can_extend_research_features("none", "i1_history")` rejects before that transformation can run. The smallest conditional source change, if history is selected, is to permit exactly the `none` → `i1_history` extension while retaining the existing name-prefix and state-shape checks. Do not broaden other parent/child combinations by assumption.
+
+`setup_model.load_initializer` requires `--inherit-init-preprocessing` for this extension and inserts the new columns at index 211. This keeps the first 211 inputs and their stored mean/std exact, inserts 156 zero projection columns, and initializes the added normalization to mean 0/std 1. The history prior is fitted from a deterministic, uniform 64-group sample of the child’s fit membership (`seed + 20261012`) in `setup_preprocessing`; it is not copied from the no-feature parent. +The current dynamics screen is explicitly cold-only: [`validation_inputs.py`](../../../src/wnn/training/validation_inputs.py#L30) rejects `--init` and teacher-cache options, and requires the 367-slot all-zero `i1_history` control. `RNNModel` adds a 52-output head and two 52-wide target-normalization buffers when enabled; ordinary outputs are concatenated with the auxiliary predictions only in training mode ([`nn.py`](../../../src/wnn/nn.py#L154)). +A warm parent without that head does not load strictly today: `setup_model.load_initializer` calls `load_state_dict` on the child state, while the parent lacks `dynamics_aux_head.*` and the two target buffers. The current screen also rejects `--init`, distillation/cache inputs, and standard auxiliary losses in [`validation_inputs.py`](../../../src/wnn/training/validation_inputs.py#L30); [`setup_model.py`](../../../src/wnn/training/setup_model.py#L108) requires exactly two pre-dynamics outputs. The F0/F1 parents have 23 readout rows with structure/next auxiliaries, and their continuation controls reuse distillation caches, so a warm dynamics continuation cannot be enabled by merely allowing one new state-dict key. If selected later, it needs a separate, tightly scoped warm mode that preserves the exact parent readout/cache recipe in both arms, places `dynamics_at` after the parent outputs, allows only the intended new head and two buffers, and rejects every other missing, unexpected or shape-mismatched tensor. +# KalmanNet-inspired innovation-conditioned GRU: source assessment
+
+## Primary sources
+
+- [KalmanNet: Neural Network Aided Kalman Filtering for Partially Known Dynamics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.10043) motivates estimating a gain from state-estimation error and measurement innovation while preserving a predictor/corrector structure. Its reported tasks have an explicit state-space interpretation.
+- [Recursive KalmanNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.11639) explores recursive neural state-estimation updates. Its preprint results are not on this competition or its anonymous market-state regression targets.
+- [KARNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14644) is a neighboring learned-filtering proposal and supplies no local transfer evidence.
+
+## Transfer assessment
+
+These papers motivate an operator-level hypothesis: predict a latent observation, measure its innovation, and learn a bounded correction gain. They do not show that this task's latent channels are physical states, that covariance is identifiable, or that the operator improves the competition's weighted Pearson objective.
+
+The proposed adapter has no calibrated process/measurement covariance recursion, observed state labels, or inference-time weight update. It is accurately described as a **KalmanNet-inspired latent observer**, not a calibrated Kalman filter or test-time-learning system. A context-only gain control masks innovation from the gain network but still applies the gain-times-innovation correction; the contrast isolates the gain's innovation conditioning only.
+
+Nearby local results are limited: fixed output filters lost on exposed F0; an additive groupwise-state ridge proxy lost on all-train rows; recurrent append deltas changed sign across two fit seeds on exposed F0; and a selected fixed local-trend input replacement showed a small uncertain positive point. These results motivate a distinct learned latent update but do not establish expected benefit.
+

+
+The local code review required prefix/chunk/reset/batch-isolation invariants, a full-shape strict-FP32 B300 profile, and a frozen clean per-cell teacher-source registry before any fit. A matched student comparison must keep the ordinary GRU endpoint, cache ancestry, coefficients and budget fixed. None has been run. No external data, pretrained weights, score, runtime or performance result is imported from these sources.

+# Variance weighting as a conditional NLL diagnostic
+
+## Question or claim
+
+Does learned residual variance change which observations receive useful mean
+updates, and interact with global clipping in the running GRU comparison?
+This is a possible explanation, not an observed quality failure.
+
+## Mechanism and method
+
+Seitzer, Tavakoli, Antić and Martius (ICLR2022) demonstrate poor mean fits under
+Gaussian likelihood optimization and analyze inverse-variance gradient weighting.
+Their beta-NLL attenuates this dependence. This is external evidence from other
+tasks, not evidence of a GRU or competition gain.
+[Primary paper, sections3–4](https://arxiv.org/html/2203.09168).
+
+The authors' implementation multiplies each NLL contribution by detached
+predicted variance raised to beta. Detachment is necessary to preserve their
+gradient prescription. [Author implementation, pinned revision](https://github.com/martius-lab/beta-nll/blob/669c9f251eb41464c1ec8b43751c7c742dd75cf9/README.md#quick-implementation-of-beta-nll).
+No external code was imported or executed.
+
+For our loss, let `s=clamp(log_variance,-4,4)`, residual `r=mean-target`, and
+`W=sum(weights)`. The current mean derivative is `2*w*exp(-s)*r/W`.
+A detached `exp(beta*s)` multiplier changes this to
+`2*w*exp((beta-1)*s)*r/W`. At beta0.5, the variance-dependent factor ranges
+from0.1353to7.3891, versus0.0183to54.5982 at beta0. These are analytical
+bounds from our clamp, not measured distributions. Keep the original weight
+denominator and scalar convention when defining a future comparison.
+
+## Evidence and interpretation
+
+The [matched epoch0 receipt](../../campaign_2026-10-20/submission_delivery_r1/nll_adaptation/nll_epoch0_diagnostics_r1.json)
+records100%NLL clipping with mean factor0.0418, versus0.9866 for WMSE. Its
+aggregate head gradient includes mean, auxiliary and variance rows; it cannot
+identify the responsible rows or establish a paper-specific failure mode.
+Global clipping rescales all gradients, while AdamW's moments also respond to
+that scaling. A small clip factor alone does not quantify the resulting
+parameter updates or prove that recurrent learning is suppressed.
+
+## Limits and validity
+
+Our variance estimates describe residual scale for a teacher/label mixture;
+they are not established estimates of irreducible market noise. At beta1,
+the direct mean derivative matches WMSE, but shared-trunk variance gradients,
+auxiliary losses and clipping can still change training.
+
+## Decision and next step
+
+Finish and grade the frozen beta0/WMSE pair first. If its quality and gradient
+diagnostics justify a new branch, a single fixed beta0.5 treatment with exact
+compatible controls could discriminate gradient weighting from the broader
+heteroscedastic hypothesis. Its allocation and recipe would need explicit
+freezing; no fit, implementation, sweep or PR is admitted by this source note.

+# From-scratch causal geometry/discrete feature comparison R4

+## Question and current status
+
+R4 compares a from-scratch H512×1 GRU with the 60 causal geometry/discrete
+features against a matched-width copy whose 60-channel suffix is zeroed. The
+feature family contains running moments, fitted arc residuals, anchor occupancy,
+exact-level identity/occupancy, event dominance and dwell. The fitting prior
+is learned from eligible fitting sequences only. Both arms use the same seed,
+source-qualified membership, model initialization, training order and fixed
+training schedule. The detailed preregistration is the
+[campaign plan](../../campaign_2026-10-17/geometry_from_scratch_r4/plan.json).
+
+**Status: attempt R4 passed fresh resource admission and started pair 0's
+fold-0 seed-42000 control fit at 2026-10-17 21:27:24 UTC. Startup source,
+input and split verification passed; no R4 score is recorded yet.** Attempts R1
+and R2 stopped before fitting due to entrypoint and input-hash errors; R3 was
+rejected while the periodic monitor held a full-core reservation. All three
+have zero fits and zero OOM events. Admission R3 binds the corrected identities.
+The user requested training both arms and a comparison relevant to
+whether this feature family merits a submission path. All 30 paired seed/fold
+runs are planned; early scores do not stop the direction. The campaign README links the preserved

+443–505 valid sequences. Folds 0 and 1 have been used in prior geometry work;
+all folds are labeled exposed or potentially exposed development evidence.

+## Recipe and evidence to collect
+
+The fixed comparison uses H512×1, FP32, AdamW, OneCycle, weighted MSE, batch 8,
+2,000-row chunks and three complete epochs. The frozen plan records fold-specific
+budgets of 44,760, 44,790, 44,850 and 44,640 optimizer updates for folds 0–3.
+Epoch 2 is graded for both arms; no best-seed choice is allowed. Each completed
+epoch saves an atomic continuation state. Thirty same-seed, same-fold pairs (60 fits) are
+balanced over four folds (8, 8, 7, 7). Per-fit provenance must show equal
+initial parameter hashes within each pair. Every run records training loss,
+learning rate, gradient norms, updates, time and fixed endpoint predictions
+with group IDs and hashes. Targets and masks are read from the hash-bound shared
+`valid_targets.npz`, not duplicated for each run.

+The first resource attempt failed argument validation because it omitted
+`--no-eval-during-fit`; it performed no optimizer updates and is preserved as a
+preflight failure. The corrected five-batch profile passed: 60/60 finite
+updates, 2.71 GB cgroup peak under the 5,000,000,000-byte cap, 0.91 GB CUDA
+allocated and 1.29 GB reserved peaks, 1.53 seconds per batch of eight full
+sequences, and no new OOM events. The separate predictor smoke exported finite
+FP32 outputs for all 468 fold-0 evaluation groups and verified their order and
+split identity. This fixes a prior-loading omission in `predict_run.py` for the
+new feature mode. The current runtime estimate is 113.8 GPU-hours for training,
+plus setup and evaluation exports; runs will execute one at a time with one
+CPU core and no swap.
+
+The primary effect is the equally weighted mean of the four fold-level paired
+`global_wp_clip2_v1` deltas. Report all paired deltas, a fold-stratified seed
+interval, and component-cluster uncertainty on fixed predictions separately.
+An interval that includes zero means uncertainty at this evidence level, not a
+reason to drop the family. A +0.001 absolute WP difference is a useful-effect
+reference, not a universal decision threshold. This comparison can establish
+only a local exposed-CV result; it does not estimate public score transfer or
+feature value in a teacher/student blend.

+# Early-to-late sequence-level expert preference R1
+
+## Question or claim
+
+Does choosing between frozen TL3 and R3 predictions for each sequence and
+target using early labels preserve an advantage on later rows, enough to
+motivate a feature-derived expert router or preference teacher?
+
+## Mechanism and method
+
+The frozen diagnostic uses all 468 F0 groups (141 connected components). It
+selects TL3 or R3 by local official weighted-Pearson score on rows 99–4,999,
+then holds that choice fixed on rows 5,000–19,999. Controls are TL3, R3, and a
+fixed 75/25 TL3/R3 mixture; a late-label hindsight selector is descriptive.
+The metric and mask are `global_wp_clip2_v1`. No model was fit.
+
+## Evidence and interpretation
+
+The early selector reached 0.714842 WP on its selection segment, only
+0.000212 above TL3 there. Its later score was 0.693871:
+
+| Late endpoint | WP |
+|---|---:|
+| TL3 | 0.697669 |
+| R3 | 0.679802 |
+| Fixed 75/25 TL3/R3 | 0.694457 |
+| Early-label selector | 0.693871 |
+| Late-label hindsight selector | 0.696703 |
+
+The early-label selector was −0.003798 versus TL3, with a paired conditional
+component-bootstrap 95% interval [−0.005690, −0.001453]. It was −0.000587
+versus the fixed 75/25 blend, with interval [−0.002360, +0.001586]. The
+hindsight selector also scored below TL3; it is not a formal upper bound under
+the globally pooled metric. The first comparison is negative for this fixed
+selector on this panel; the second remains uncertain rather than a proven
+loss.
+
+The selected R3 rate fell from 21.6%/24.8% early to 14.5%/13.0% late for the
+two targets. Early/late identity agreement was 68.16% for both. As a
+post-hoc descriptive baseline, independent choices with those marginal rates
+would agree about 70.16% and 68.64%; raw agreement therefore does not show
+positive persistence beyond the TL3-dominated base rates. This comparison has
+no uncertainty interval and is not a significance test.
+
+An independent result review confirmed the score and interval alignment and
+requested that the marginal-agreement baseline accompany the result. The
+pre-grade static review passed source, timing, metric, and bootstrap checks.
+
+## Limits and validity
+
+F0 is repeatedly exposed, R3 was selected using F0, and TL3 ancestry is
+unknown. Choices use validation labels unavailable to the test callback, so
+this is not an online policy. The component intervals condition on cached
+predictions and selected early choices; they do not measure fitting seeds,
+clean folds, feedback maturity, or public transfer. The late hindsight result
+is not a formal pooled-metric oracle bound. The result narrows these two fixed
+experts and this label-informed selector only; it does not reject broader
+causal online learning or learned state features.
+
+The eight-group memory profile processed eight F0 groups but materialized the
+full target and mask arrays from the compressed validation NPZ. Both this
+profile and the full grade ran under a 2 GB worker reservation with zero OOM
+counter deltas. Profile cgroup peak was 533,319,680 bytes; grade cgroup peak
+was 387,665,920 bytes and process RSS was 569,810,944 bytes. The profile's
+whole-archive SHA matched again before the full grade.
+
+## Decision and next step
+
+Do not create a separate B300 expert-router draft from this result: the
+label-informed selector has no later advantage, its agreement is explained by
+the dominant TL3 choice, and no label-blind input signal has been shown to
+predict useful choices. Keep the larger retained-raw Kalman feature
+teacher/student proposal in existing [draft PR #17](https://github.com/VladKochetov007/WunderFunder/pull/17)
+as a distinct, still-unprofiled direction. This screen does not close online
+learning with verified mature feedback or causal learned-state features.

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import json
+import subprocess
+import zipfile
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+LEVELS = {
+    "v2": "-C target-cpu=x86-64-v2",
+    "avx2": "-C target-cpu=x86-64 -C target-feature=+avx2,+fma",
+    "v3": "-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3",
+}
+
+
+def source_hashes() -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Bind a native build to its Rust sources, lockfile and build definition."""
+    paths = [ROOT / "native" / name for name in ("Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock")]
+    paths += sorted((ROOT / "native" / "src").rglob("*.rs"))
+    paths += [
+        ROOT / "submission" / "Dockerfile.build",
+        ROOT / "scripts" / "check_submission_abi.py",
+        Path(__file__).resolve(),
+    ]
+    return {
+        path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(): hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+        for path in paths
+    }
+
+
+def run(command: list[str]) -> None:
+    """Run a build command; propagate failure without starting any model code."""
+    subprocess.run(command, check=True, cwd=ROOT)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    """Compile Linux x86-64 libraries and inspect ELF metadata, without inference."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--image", default="wnn-i1-history-build:20261023")
+    parser.add_argument("--skip-image-build", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    output = args.output.resolve()
+    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
+    sources = source_hashes()
+    if not args.skip_image_build:
+        run(
+            [
+                "docker",
+                "build",
+                "--platform",
+                "linux/amd64",
+                "-t",
+                args.image,
+                "-f",
+                str(ROOT / "submission" / "Dockerfile.build"),
+                str(ROOT / "submission"),
+            ]
+        )
+    image_id = subprocess.check_output(
+        ["docker", "image", "inspect", "--format", "{{.Id}}", args.image], text=True
+    ).strip()
+    for level, flags in LEVELS.items():
+        run(
+            [
+                "docker",
+                "run",
+                "--rm",
+                "--platform",
+                "linux/amd64",
+                "--cpus",
+                "1",
+                "--memory",
+                "2g",
+                "--memory-swap",
+                "2g",
+                "-e",
+                "CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=1",
+                "-e",
+                "CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/out/target",
+                "-e",
+                f"RUSTFLAGS={flags}",
+                "-v",
+                f"{ROOT / 'native'}:/src:ro",
+                "-v",
+                f"{output}:/out",
+                args.image,
+                "maturin",
+                "build",
+                "--locked",
+                "--release",
+                "--features",
+                "extension-module",
+                "-m",
+                "/src/Cargo.toml",
+                "-o",
+                f"/out/wheel/{level}",
+            ]
+        )
+        wheels = list((output / "wheel" / level).glob("wnn_native-*.whl"))
+        if len(wheels) != 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"expected exactly one wheel for {level}")
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(wheels[0]) as wheel:
+            libraries = [n for n in wheel.namelist() if n.endswith("wnn_native.abi3.so")]
+            if len(libraries) != 1:
+                raise ValueError(f"expected exactly one abi3 library for {level}")
+            destination = output / level / "wnn_native.abi3.so"
+            destination.parent.mkdir()
+            destination.write_bytes(wheel.read(libraries[0]))
+    if sources != source_hashes():
+        raise ValueError("native sources changed during compilation; rebuild in a new directory")
+    # Run only the stdlib/readelf inspector. It never imports the native library.
+    run(
+        [
+            "docker",
+            "run",
+            "--rm",
+            "--platform",
+            "linux/amd64",
+            "--network",
+            "none",
+            "--cpus",
+            "1",
+            "--memory",
+            "256m",
+            "--memory-swap",
+            "256m",
+            "-v",
+            f"{ROOT / 'scripts' / 'check_submission_abi.py'}:/inspect.py:ro",
+            "-v",
+            f"{output}:/out",
+            *[
+                item
+                for level in LEVELS
+                for item in ("-v", f"{output / level}:/artifact/{level}:ro")
+            ],
+            args.image,
+            "python",
+            "/inspect.py",
+            "/artifact",
+            "--output",
+            "/out/STATIC_ABI.json",
+        ]
+    )
+    abi = json.loads((output / "STATIC_ABI.json").read_text())
+    library_hashes = {
+        f"{level}/wnn_native.abi3.so": hashlib.sha256(
+            (output / level / "wnn_native.abi3.so").read_bytes()
+        ).hexdigest()
+        for level in LEVELS
+    }
+    receipt = {
+        "schema": "wnn.i1-native-build.v1",
+        "image_id": image_id,
+        "platform": "linux/amd64",
+        "source_hashes": sources,
+        "library_hashes": library_hashes,
+        "static_abi": abi,
+        "inference_executed": False,
+        "tests_executed": False,
+        "training_executed": False,
+        "runtime_and_parity": "not_tested",
+    }
+    (output / "NATIVE_BUILD.json").write_text(json.dumps(receipt, indent=2) + "\n")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
